findings.title: Auditor is instructed to apply the confidence cap but is denied the classification data the cap depends on
findings.impact: Reader trust and review-queue signal quality. The auditor's instructions require capping confidence at low when the source pool is classified claimed/self-reported, but SourceContext and the prompt omit every source's independence and kind. The LLM must re-guess pool classification from publisher strings, so cap application is inconsistent with the analyst's, producing spurious confidence disagreements (needs_review noise) and spurious agreements (missed real disagreements).
findings.current: auditor/instructions.md tells the model to apply the same cap as the analyst for pools 'classified claimed or self-reported'. But ClaimBundle's SourceContext carries only id/title/publisher/summary/key_quotes/body, and build_auditor_prompt renders only publisher/summary/quotes/body. The effective independence and kind values (which the analyst DOES receive, including source_overrides effects) never reach the auditor. SourceContext.id is populated but never rendered either.
findings.proposed: Add independence and kind to SourceContext and render them in build_auditor_prompt (they are facts about sources, not analyst conclusions, so information asymmetry is preserved). Better still: compute the cap mechanically. The claimed/self-reported derivation is a pure function of the pool; compute it once in compare() or bundle.py and clamp both assessments before diffing, leaving the LLM only the judgment calls.
findings.migration: 1) Add independence/kind fields to SourceContext and thread them through build_bundle and the cli step-audit inline construction. 2) Render both lines in build_auditor_prompt next to Publisher. 3) Move the cap sentence in auditor/instructions.md from 'infer the pool class' to 'the pool class is given per source'. 4) Add a compare() test asserting cap parity between primary and assessed confidence for an all-first-party pool.

verification.note: Facts verified: SourceContext lacks independence/kind, build_auditor_prompt renders neither, id unrendered. But the instructions give a content-based fallback definition of the cap, and per compare.py confidence disagreement alone never sets needs_review, so the review-queue harm is overstated.
verification.simpler_alternative: Thread independence/kind into SourceContext and render two prompt lines; drop the mechanical clamp — claimed/self-reported is not a pure function (first-party-article upgrade needs judgment) and clamping via analyst source_overrides leaks analyst conclusions into the 'independent' assessment.

findings.title: CLI step commands fork the agent invocation paths: divergent prompts, timeouts, slugs, validation, and retry policy
findings.impact: Anyone touching ingest or audit behavior must change two places or silently diverge them further. Concretely today: the pipeline path (the one that writes production files) never runs validate_source_file; the CLI path never applies the slug_from_url override, so the same URL yields different filenames depending on entry point; step-ingest hardcodes a 120s timeout while the pipeline uses cfg.ingest_timeout_s; step-audit runs the auditor with no timeout and no Infomaniak null-body retry, so gateway blips that the pipeline tolerates crash the CLI.
findings.current: cli.py step-ingest re-implements _ingest_one: the same prompt string is duplicated verbatim, the CLI adds validation the pipeline lacks, the pipeline adds a slug override the CLI lacks. cli.py step-audit calls auditor_agent.run(prompt) bare while pipeline.py wraps the identical call in _run_with_null_retry with cfg.auditor_timeout_s.
findings.proposed: One invocation function per agent, owned by the agent package: ingest_url(client, url, cfg-ish opts) -> SourceFile that builds the prompt, applies timeout, runs semantic validation, and applies the slug policy; audit_bundle(bundle, model, timeout) that owns null-retry. Both the pipeline and the CLI call these; the CLI keeps only argument parsing and printing.
findings.migration: 1) Extract _ingest_one's prompt/run/slug/validation core into pipeline/ingestor (it currently lives in the orchestrator). 2) Rewrite step-ingest to call it; delete the duplicated prompt string and the hardcoded 120. 3) Extract the _run_with_null_retry + override wrapper for the auditor into a small run helper and call it from step-audit. 4) Add a test that the two entry points produce identical slugs and identical validation outcomes for a fixture page.

evidence.quote: Ingest this URL and produce a SourceFile
Ingest this URL and produce a SourceFile

verification.note: All divergences verified: pipeline never runs validate_source_file, CLI never applies slug_from_url override, CLI hardcodes 120s vs cfg default (wayback-derived or 60s), step-audit runs bare with no timeout and no null-body retry. Real dual-path fork on code that writes production files.
verification.simpler_alternative: Have step-ingest call the existing _ingest_one (minimal VerifyConfig + Semaphore(1)) and extract pipeline's auditor override+null-retry block into a helper step-audit also calls — reuses orchestrator code without relocating invocation cores into the agent packages.

findings.title: Analyst instructions and field description say entity_type 'topic' but the enum value is 'subject'
findings.impact: The LLM receives contradictory guidance: the JSON schema it must satisfy allows company/product/subject, while the prose (both instructions.md and the Field description embedded in the schema) says 'topic'. Models that follow the prose emit 'topic', fail enum validation, and burn the 2-retry budget; on small Infomaniak models this converts to analyst failures and blocked claims.
findings.current: analyst/instructions.md defines entity_type as company/product/topic and elaborates the 'topic' case with an example; EntityResolution.entity_type's description repeats 'One of: company, product, topic'. common/models.py EntityType has SUBJECT = "subject" (matching the Zod schema per enum-drift, which shows EntityType in sync across Python and TS).
findings.proposed: Instructions and Field descriptions should be generated from, or asserted against, the enum. Minimum fix: replace 'topic' with 'subject' in both places. Better: a unit test that greps each agent's instructions.md for every enum literal it names and fails on values absent from the enum (same class of check the enum-drift report already does cross-language).
findings.migration: 1) Fix the two 'topic' strings. 2) Add a test asserting each documented entity_type value is a valid EntityType. 3) Re-run a small claim batch to confirm retry counts drop.

verification.note: Verified: instructions.md:13 and the Field description both say 'topic'; EntityType is company/product/subject and in sync with the Zod schema. The no-entity-ref path (research_claim with resolved_entity=None) exercises LLM entity resolution, so the schema-violating prose is reachable.

findings.title: SourceKind 'paper' exists in both schemas but no agent instructions mention it, and the verification-level derivation has no bucket for it
findings.impact: The ingestor will never label an arXiv paper kind: paper (it is told the kind vocabulary is seven values), so academic sources get misfiled as report/article. Worse, the analyst's verification_level rules put first-party kinds into either {report, documentation, dataset} (self-reported) or {blog, index, video, article} (claimed); 'paper' belongs to neither set, so a first-party paper has an undefined derivation the LLM resolves arbitrarily.
findings.current: common/models.py SourceKind includes PAPER (in sync with content.config.ts per enum-drift). ingestor/instructions.md line 15 lists only the original seven kinds. analyst/instructions.md's two derivation buckets also enumerate only the original seven.
findings.proposed: Add paper to the ingestor's kind list and assign it explicitly in the analyst's derivation buckets (a first-party paper with methodology plausibly belongs with report/documentation/dataset in self-reported). Cover both with the enum-literals-in-instructions test proposed in AT-03 so the next enum addition cannot silently skip the prompts.
findings.migration: 1) Add paper to ingestor/instructions.md kind list. 2) Add paper to the self-reported bucket in analyst/instructions.md and to the SOURCE QUALITY kind list. 3) Extend the instructions-vs-enum test to require every SourceKind value appears in both files.

evidence.quote: kind: one of: report, article, documentation, dataset, blog, video, index

verification.note: Both sides verified: SourceKind.PAPER in both schemas; ingestor instructions list 7 kinds; analyst derivation buckets and kind list omit paper, so a first-party paper has undefined derivation. 'Never labels paper' slightly overstates (schema still allows it), making the gap more likely, not less.

findings.title: Ingestor validation is half-dead: unused parameters, a quote check that never runs, a duplicate slug check, and zero tests
findings.impact: The module advertises five semantic checks but delivers three in one entry point only. The key-quote fabrication check (the highest-value check for a site whose content rules forbid invented quotes) never executes because no caller passes page_text. Maintenance cost without the protection.
findings.current: validate_source_file takes repo_root, which no check reads. Its only caller (cli.py step-ingest) passes three positional args, so page_text is always None and _check_key_quotes is unreachable in practice. _check_slug_format re-validates the identical regex Pydantic already enforces on SourceFile.slug, so it can never fire. _check_year_plausibility calls datetime.date.today() directly even though IngestorDeps carries an injected today. IngestorDeps.repo_root is likewise required but never read by any tool. No file in pipeline/tests references ingestor.validation.
findings.proposed: Fold validation into the single ingest entry point from AT-02 and run it on both paths. Pass the fetched page text through so the quote check actually runs (the web_fetch tool already has it). Delete the redundant slug check, the repo_root parameters (both here and on IngestorDeps), and inject the clock. Add tests for the surviving checks, especially quote-not-found warnings.
findings.migration: 1) Delete repo_root from validate_source_file and IngestorDeps; fix the two construction sites. 2) Capture page text from the last successful web_fetch (e.g., stash on deps) and pass it to validation in the shared ingest path. 3) Remove _check_slug_format; keep the Pydantic pattern as the single enforcement. 4) Add pipeline/tests/test_ingestor_validation.py covering each check.

verification.note: Verified: sole caller is cli step-ingest with page_text=None, zero tests, repo_root unused in both places. Nuance: pipeline mutates sf.slug post-construction without re-validation (no validate_assignment), so if validation moves to both paths per AT-02, don't delete the slug check blindly.

findings.title: The orchestrator-to-agent source contract is a stringly-typed dict with two competing key vocabularies
findings.impact: A key typo fails silently: build_analyst_prompt uses src.get(...) for kind/independence/addresses/source_id, so a misspelled key just drops that line from the prompt with no error, quietly degrading verdicts (e.g., losing 'addresses' disables the sub-question coverage rules). The auditor's build_bundle expects 'slug' while the analyst expects 'source_id' from the same dict, so every producer must know both vocabularies.
findings.current: _build_source_dict in the orchestrator emits a 10-key dict; build_analyst_prompt(sources: list[dict]) reads title/publisher/kind/independence/addresses/summary/key_quotes/body/source_id via mixed [] and .get(); auditor/bundle.py reads slug/title/publisher/summary/key_quotes/body. There is no shared type, so nothing verifies the producer and two consumers agree.
findings.proposed: One shared Pydantic model (e.g., common.models.SourcePacket) with the union of fields, produced once by the orchestrator and accepted by both prompt builders. Required fields become constructor-enforced; optional prompt sections key off typed Optionals instead of dict.get. This also gives the auditor its missing independence/kind for free (AT-01).
findings.migration: 1) Define SourcePacket in common/models.py mirroring _build_source_dict's keys. 2) Change build_analyst_prompt and build_bundle signatures to list[SourcePacket]; delete the dict indexing. 3) Update _build_source_dict to return SourcePacket and the cli step-audit source loading to construct it. 4) Delete the 'slug' vs 'source_id' duality (keep source_id; derive slug where needed).

verification.note: Verified: _build_source_dict emits 10 keys; analyst reads via mixed []/.get; bundle expects 'slug' vs analyst 'source_id'; 'addresses' is patched in at 4 separate pipeline.py sites, confirming every producer must know the vocabulary. Silent-drop-on-typo behavior is real.

findings.title: analyst/agent.py mixes four concerns in one file while its two siblings use split layouts
findings.impact: The analyst is the highest-churn, highest-complexity file of the trio (churn 17 commits, ccn_max 20, hotspot rank 16), and every kind of change (prompt tweak, output-schema change, markdown-hygiene fix, truncation heuristic) lands in the same 313-line file, maximizing merge collisions and review noise. The three agents having three different layouts (analyst: everything in agent.py; auditor: agent/models/bundle/compare/report; ingestor: agent/models/validation/tools) means there is no place a contributor can predict a given concern lives.
findings.current: One file contains: _surround_lists_with_blanks (markdownlint MD032 repair), _reject_if_truncated (generic truncation heuristics), four Pydantic models with validators, two module-level Agent instances, and build_analyst_prompt (the trio's longest function).
findings.proposed: Adopt the auditor's layout as the trio-wide convention: analyst/models.py (EntityResolution, SourceOverride, VerdictAssessment, AnalystOutput and their validators), analyst/agent.py (agent instances only), analyst/prompt.py (build_analyst_prompt). Move _surround_lists_with_blanks and _reject_if_truncated to common/ as generic LLM-output hygiene; they are not analyst-specific and would apply to any future markdown-emitting agent.
findings.migration: 1) Move the two text helpers to common/text_hygiene.py with their existing tests. 2) Split models into analyst/models.py; keep re-exports in agent.py for one release to avoid breaking orchestrator imports. 3) Move build_analyst_prompt to analyst/prompt.py. 4) Update the orchestrator imports and drop the re-exports.

verification.note: Metrics verified (313 loc, churn 17, ccn_max 20, hotspot rank 16) and the three-layout asymmetry is real. But the impact is developer friction only; merge-collision/review-noise framing overstates it in a single-maintainer repo. Consistency cleanup, not medium-severity risk.

findings.title: All four Agent singletons are built with the 'test' placeholder model, so a forgotten override silently fabricates data
findings.impact: In PydanticAI the string 'test' is TestModel, which returns synthetic output that satisfies the schema. Every call site must remember to wrap the run in agent.override(model=resolve_model(...)); a call site that forgets does not crash, it produces a fabricated SourceFile or verdict that type-checks and flows into research/ files. For a fact-checking site, silently fabricated output is the worst possible failure mode, and today only convention prevents it.
findings.current: analyst_agent, verdict_only_agent, auditor_agent, and ingestor_agent are all module-level Agent("test", ...) instances; the orchestrator and CLI wrap each run in .override(model=resolve_model(spec)). Instructions files are also read at import time, so importing any agent module touches the filesystem.
findings.proposed: Pass the model per run instead of per agent: PydanticAI's run() accepts model=. Give each agent package a run helper (run_analyst(prompt, model, timeout)) that requires a model argument, and construct the Agent with model=None so an un-modeled run raises instead of fabricating. The override dance disappears and the failure mode becomes loud.
findings.migration: 1) Change the four Agent constructions to model=None. 2) Replace each 'with X.override(model=...)' block with model= passed to run() inside the shared null-retry helper. 3) Keep .override(model=TestModel()) usage in tests only. 4) Grep CI for 'override(model=' outside tests to hold the line.
findings.evidence_note: 3/4 evidence entries failed grep and were disregarded

verification.note: Verified in the project venv: infer_model('test') returns TestModel; all 4 singletons use it, undocumented; 8 override sites are the only guard. Latent (no current site forgets), but AT-02 shows new hand-rolled invocation sites do get added, and the failure mode is silent schema-valid fabrication.

findings.title: build_bundle fabricates claim_id from the entity name, and the CLI bypasses the factory entirely
findings.impact: Two claims about the same entity get the identical synthetic id 'verify/<entity-slug>' in reports and comparisons, so a batch verify run's auditor report cannot distinguish them. Meanwhile step-audit constructs ClaimBundle inline with the real claim id, meaning the factory that claims 'the auditor owns the mapping to its internal types' covers only one of the two construction sites, and any bundle-shape change must be made twice.
findings.current: bundle.py hardcodes claim_id=f"verify/{slugify(entity_name)}" because the pipeline path runs before the claim file exists; cli.py step-audit builds ClaimBundle/EntityContext/SourceContext by hand from loaded frontmatter.
findings.proposed: Make claim_id a required parameter of build_bundle (the pipeline can pass its provisional verify/<slug>-<criteria> identity, which it already knows), and use build_bundle from step-audit. One construction path, and disambiguated ids in batch reports.
findings.migration: 1) Add claim_id param to build_bundle; delete the slugify fabrication. 2) Call build_bundle from step-audit with the file-derived id. 3) Align the source dict keys via AT-06's SourcePacket.

verification.note: Verified: bundle.py fabricates verify/<entity-slug>, so two claims for one entity collide in batch reports and comparisons; step-audit builds ClaimBundle inline with the real claim id, bypassing the factory. Low is right — operator-facing report ambiguity only.

findings.title: compare.py's off-scale handling documents unverified but silently lumps not-applicable in with it
findings.impact: Maintainers reading VERDICT_ORDER's comment believe unverified is the only off-scale verdict, but Verdict.NOT_APPLICABLE is equally unmapped: any disagreement involving either value collapses to MAJOR severity via the ordinal-is-None branch. An 'unverified vs not-applicable' split (both agents saying the claim cannot be scored, for different reasons) is flagged with the same severity as 'true vs false minus one'.
findings.current: VERDICT_ORDER maps the five scored verdicts; the trailing comment says only 'Verdict.UNVERIFIED is off-scale -- handled separately'. _verdict_severity returns MAJOR for any None ordinal.
findings.proposed: Handle the off-scale pair explicitly: same-off-scale pairs (unverified vs not-applicable) should get their own severity (or ADJACENT), and the comment should name both values. Consider an OFF_SCALE member on VerdictSeverity if the review queue wants to triage these differently from real polarity disagreements.
findings.migration: 1) Extend _verdict_severity with an explicit both-off-scale branch. 2) Fix the comment to name both off-scale values. 3) Add compare() tests for unverified/not-applicable pairings.

verification.note: Verified: the VERDICT_ORDER comment names only UNVERIFIED; NOT_APPLICABLE is equally unmapped, and any differing pair involving either yields MAJOR (hence needs_review). unverified-vs-not-applicable is a live combination since both are valid LLM outputs of the Verdict enum.

findings.title: Auditor/Evaluator naming split is now baked into persisted artifacts; flipping the docs is cheaper than the planned code rename
findings.impact: Every new sidecar written deepens the cost of the deferred rename: 'auditor' is persisted in .audit.yaml keys (agents_run, models_used), encoded in the AgentName literal and VerifyConfig fields, in CLI command/flag names (step-audit, --auditor-model), and in the dr-debug-blocked skill, while the docs and the Phase enum say Evaluator/evaluating. Contributors grep for one name and miss half the call sites.
findings.current: AGENTS.md declares the role Evaluator with the rename to evaluator/ deferred post-v1; orchestrator/__init__.py carries a reconciliation note; the claim lifecycle phase is 'evaluating'; but code, CLI, config, sidecar data, and the agents_run lineage all say auditor.
findings.proposed: Decide the canonical name now and make it the code's name: rename the ROLE in docs to Auditor (a handful of prose edits in AGENTS.md and two module docstrings) instead of renaming the package, CLI, config fields, and migrating persisted sidecar values to evaluator. Rename Phase.EVALUATING to auditing only if claim frontmatter migration is acceptable; otherwise document phase 'evaluating' as the one legacy spelling. Either way, stop carrying a planned rename that grows more expensive with every published claim.
findings.migration: 1) Decision: canonical = auditor. 2) Edit AGENTS.md role table and narrative (Evaluator -> Auditor, keep one parenthetical alias). 3) Delete the deferred-rename notes in orchestrator/__init__.py and AGENTS.md line 128. 4) Leave Phase.EVALUATING as-is with a one-line comment, or migrate it in the same release as the next sidecar schema_version bump.

evidence.quote: auditor/         # Evaluator role; directory rename to evaluator/ deferred to post-v1

verification.note: Both sides verified: AGENTS.md lines 118/128 and orchestrator/__init__ say Evaluator; code, CLI, VerifyConfig, AgentName, and persisted agents_run/models_used say auditor; Phase.EVALUATING persists in frontmatter. Extends KF-07 with a real accumulating-cost argument; docs-flip direction is sound.

findings.title: independence has two uncoordinated writers: the ingestor LLM (with zero guidance) and a publisher-string classifier default
findings.impact: independence drives the verification_level and the low-confidence cap, i.e., the site's core trust signal. Yet the ingestor's output schema exposes the field while its instructions never mention it, so the LLM fills it by guesswork; only when the LLM leaves it empty does the deterministic classifier (independence <- source_type <- publisher+kind) supply a value. Two writers with different logic on the reader-facing trust axis, and 3 of 36 committed sources still lack the field.
findings.current: SourceFrontmatter.independence is Optional and undocumented in ingestor/instructions.md (the frontmatter list ends at key_quotes). pipeline.py's _build_source_dict and cli.py's step-ingest both default it from classify_source_type only 'if not set', silently trusting whatever the LLM wrote. This is the agents-trio face of the four-axis problem (kind, source_type, independence, publisher_quality): the axes are derived from each other in a chain but each has an independent entry point.
findings.proposed: Pick one writer. Either (a) remove independence from SourceFrontmatter so the LLM cannot set it and the classifier is the sole author (analyst source_overrides remain the per-claim correction channel, which already exists for exactly this), or (b) keep the LLM as author but give it the first-party/independent definition in instructions.md and demote the classifier to a lint check that flags disagreement instead of silently filling gaps.
findings.migration: 1) Choose (a): drop independence from SourceFrontmatter; always stamp it in _build_source_dict/step-ingest from the classifier. 2) Backfill the 3 sources missing the field with the classifier. 3) Add a linter rule that every source carries independence. 4) Note in docs/architecture/source-quality.md that per-claim disagreement is expressed via source_overrides, not by editing the source file.

evidence.quote: - key_quotes: 0-5 notable direct quotes from the source (optional)

verification.note: Verified: independence is exposed in SourceFrontmatter but absent from the instructions' frontmatter list; both writers confirmed (LLM value trusted, classifier fills only when empty) in pipeline.py and cli.py; 3 of 36 committed sources lack the field, matching data-conformance (33/36).

findings.title: models.py is two unrelated modules fused: the enum vocabulary and the provider gateway churn together at fan-in 48
findings.impact: Every provider quirk fix (Mistral reasoning strip, gpt-oss native output, Infomaniak response logging) edits the single file that 48 modules import for stable enum values. The repo's highest fan-in file is also a top-10 hotspot, so the blast radius of gateway experiments is the whole pipeline; reviewers must re-check enum stability on every provider change.
findings.current: pipeline/common/models.py holds eleven enums, AGENT_NAMES, ACADEMIC_* constants, SubQuestion, FailureInfo, DEFAULT_MODEL, an httpx response-logging hook, and resolve_model with per-model quirk registries. Graphify already sees two communities (42 enums, 46 model resolution) inside the one file. resolve_model also constructs a fresh httpx.AsyncClient per cached spec, so two Infomaniak model ids do not share a connection pool and cache_clear() leaks clients.
findings.proposed: Split into common/enums.py (pure stdlib: enums + AGENT_NAMES + ACADEMIC_*) and common/providers.py (resolve_model, quirk predicates, DEFAULT_MODEL, the logging hook, one shared AsyncClient per base URL). Keep models.py as a re-export shim for one release, then delete it. SubQuestion and FailureInfo move to providers.py's sibling (they are pipeline-run shapes, not vocabulary).
findings.migration: 1) Create enums.py and providers.py, move code verbatim. 2) Make models.py `from .enums import *; from .providers import *` shim. 3) Mechanically rewrite the ~48 importers (sed on `from common.models import`). 4) Delete the shim and add a lint forbidding new common.models imports.

evidence.quote: Shared enums mirroring the Zod schemas in src/content.config.ts.

verification.note: Metrics verified (fan_in 48, churn 23, hotspot rank 8); 11 enums plus the gateway share one file, and each infomaniak spec builds its own AsyncClient (models.py:301) so cache_clear() does leak clients. Impact wording is slightly rhetorical but the congestion claim is metric-backed.
verification.simpler_alternative: Move only the volatile half (resolve_model, quirk predicates, _log_infomaniak_response, DEFAULT_MODEL) to common/providers.py. Only 3 production files import it (cli.py, pipeline.py, researcher/decomposed.py), so no shim, no lint rule, and no 48-importer rewrite; enums stay in models.py.

findings.title: Enum mirror to Zod is pure discipline; the repo already has the drift-guard pattern but never applied it to the 10 enum pairs
findings.impact: A value added on one side (new Category, new BlockedReason) ships silently until an Astro build rejects frontmatter, or worse, the site accepts a value the pipeline never emits. Trust in the published data rests on contributors remembering to edit two files.
findings.current: models.py declares itself a mirror of src/content.config.ts and enum-drift.json shows 10 pairs currently in sync with zero automation. Meanwhile pipeline/tests/test_entity_resolution.py already reads content.config.ts as text to drift-guard a single field and one three-value enum, proving the cheap check is feasible; it just was never extended to the enum mirror.
findings.proposed: One parametrized pytest that extracts each z.enum([...]) value set from content.config.ts (regex is enough, as the existing test argues) and asserts equality with the Python enum's values, for all 10 pairs plus a registry of intentionally py-only enums (VerdictSeverity). Full codegen is not warranted at this scale; a failing test on drift is.
findings.migration: 1) Add PY_TO_ZOD pairs table in a new test module. 2) Reuse the text-read approach from test_entity_resolution.py. 3) List VerdictSeverity as expected-py-only so the test also fails when someone mirrors it accidentally.

evidence.quote: Shared enums mirroring the Zod schemas in src/content.config.ts.

verification.note: enum-drift.json shows 10/10 pairs in sync with zero automation; test_entity_resolution.py:203 already text-reads content.config.ts to guard one field plus one enum literal set, and no other drift automation exists in tests, scripts/, or CI. VerdictSeverity is the 11th, py-only enum as claimed.

findings.title: Topic vocabulary is an enum in one place and free strings everywhere else
findings.impact: A typo'd topic slug in research/templates.yaml flows through template load, claim rendering, and list_claims topic filtering without any check, and only fails (if at all) at Astro build. The enum is also named Category while every field it populates is called topics, so readers of the code cannot grep one name.
findings.current: models.py defines `class Category(str, Enum)` with the eight kebab-case topics; templates.py types the same values as `topics: list[str]` with only a comment as the contract, and content_loader.list_claims compares raw strings.
findings.proposed: Rename Category to Topic (matching the field name the site and frontmatter actually use), then validate templates at load: TemplateRecord.__post_init__ already raises on bad subject refs, so add the same treatment for unknown topic values. list_claims stays string-based but bad input can no longer enter via templates.
findings.migration: 1) Rename Category->Topic with a Category = Topic alias for one release. 2) In load_templates, check every entry topic against Topic values and raise. 3) Drop the alias after importers are updated.

verification.note: Unvalidated at load as claimed, but the mechanism differs: pipeline wraps Category(t) in except ValueError -> [], so a typo yields topics=[] on blocked claims, failing Astro's .min(1) at build; analyst topics are enum-typed so published claims are safe. Silent-until-build endpoint still holds.

findings.title: Publisher-tier lists are hardcoded substring sets with known false-positive behavior, while the sibling blocklist is operator-editable YAML
findings.impact: Source-quality labels feed reader-facing trust signals (source_type, independence, URL scoring). Substring matching marks any publisher or hostname containing 'meta' or 'google' as primary/first-party (e.g. a 'Metaculus' publisher or metafilter.com hostname), silently inflating independence for exactly the tier the site tells readers to trust least skeptically. Extending the vocabulary requires a code change and redeploy, unlike blocklist.yaml which was explicitly designed for operator edits.
findings.current: source_classification.py hardcodes three frozensets of publisher substrings; its own comment concedes the substring false-positive problem ('sec.gov' special-cased so 'sec' does not match 'section') but leaves 'meta', 'google', 'ref'-style short tokens unguarded. publisher_quality.py then imports the private _PRIMARY_PUBLISHERS/_SECONDARY_PUBLISHERS/_TERTIARY_PUBLISHERS names across module boundaries and applies them to hostnames, a different text domain than publisher names.
findings.proposed: Move the tier vocabulary to research/source-tiers.yaml (same operator-editable pattern blocklist.py documents), loaded once with lru_cache like the blocklist. Match hostnames by registrable-domain suffix (the _host_matches helper already exists) and publishers by word-boundary token, not substring. Merge publisher_quality.py into source_classification.py so the shared lists stop being cross-module privates.

findings.title: --entity filter poisons corpus-level checks: every source and entity outside the filter is flagged as unreferenced
findings.impact: `dr lint --entity ecosia` (documented in AGENTS.md as a supported flow) computes the referenced-source set from only that entity's claims, so every other cited source in the repo is reported as 'unreferenced-source' with the hint 'remove the file' — actively dangerous advice if an operator or agent follows it, and it drowns the real per-entity issues.
findings.current: collect_all_paths filters claim files by directory name, but run_all_checks then feeds the filtered claim list into check_unreferenced_sources and check_unreferenced_entities, whose reference sets are built solely from the claims passed in. All entity/source files are still collected unfiltered, so the delta is reported as orphans.
findings.proposed: Tag checks with a scope (per-file vs corpus). When entity_filter is set, either skip corpus-scope checks (unreferenced-*, duplicate-entity-slug) or build reference sets from the full corpus and restrict only which paths get reported. The registry from LINT-04 is the natural place for the scope tag.
findings.migration: 1) Add a scope marker per check. 2) In run_all_checks, skip corpus-scope checks when entity_filter is not None (one-line guard today). 3) Add a regression test: two entities, filter on one, assert zero unreferenced-* issues. 4) Note the behavior in the dr lint help text.

findings.title: Parse failures are swallowed: malformed frontmatter lints as empty, malformed templates.yaml lints as no-templates
findings.impact: A claim with broken YAML frontmatter produces seven misleading missing-required-field errors instead of one 'unparseable' error; a malformed source file produces zero issues (silent pass, then the Astro build fails on it); a syntax error in templates.yaml makes every claim with a criteria_slug report bogus broken-criteria-slug errors. Operators debug the wrong thing each time.
findings.current: _read_frontmatter catches all exceptions and returns {}, and load_templates catches all exceptions and returns an empty slug set. Downstream checks cannot distinguish 'file is empty of fields' from 'file could not be parsed'.
findings.proposed: Emit a first-class 'unparseable-frontmatter' error issue per failing file and skip other checks for that file; treat a templates.yaml load failure as a fatal lint error (or a dedicated error issue) rather than an empty set. Never let {} stand in for parse failure.
findings.migration: 1) Change _read_frontmatter to return fm | ParseError sentinel. 2) In run_all_checks, convert sentinels to unparseable-frontmatter issues and exclude those paths from per-file checks. 3) Same treatment for load_templates. 4) Add tests with deliberately broken YAML.

verification.note: Verified both swallow sites (runner.py:42, :55-56). parse_frontmatter raises on missing delimiters or bad YAML; {} then yields 7 missing-required-field errors per broken claim, zero issues for a broken cited source (missing_independence skips when accessed_date isn't a date), and templates.yaml failure flags every slugged claim.

findings.title: Adding a check means editing three places; runner hand-lists 21 imports and 21 calls
findings.impact: checks.py is the repo's #5 hotspot (16 commits, 111 total complexity) and every new check touches checks.py, the runner's import block, and the runner's call sequence. The identical `fm = claim_frontmatters.get(str(path), {})` boilerplate is repeated in nearly every check, and severity/check_id are scattered through 21 function bodies, so there is no single place to see the check taxonomy.
findings.current: run_all_checks imports every check by name and calls each with a hand-picked subset of nine index arguments. Check metadata (id, severity) lives inline in LintIssue constructor calls inside each function.

Severity and scope become data you can list, filter, and document from one table, and LINT-02's scope guard falls out naturally.

Conversely only claim_refresh passes reset_review=True. ~200-line duplication per side, already diverged with operator-visible effect.

findings.title: Provider key preflight is bypassed by any model spec containing the substring 'test' (including 'latest')
findings.impact: The preflight exists to surface missing API keys upfront instead of as a deep SDK error mid-run. findings.title: dr publish re-implements review's gating and sidecar write; approve_claim's own sidecar mutation is unguarded and clobbers notes
findings.impact: Three publication paths (review --approve, publish, review-queue [a]) must agree on what 'publishable' means, but publish keeps its own copy of the status/criterion gate, acknowledged by a parity comment, so a new gate (e.g. a future verification_level floor) must be added twice or the bulk and single paths disagree. Separately, approve_claim indexes sidecar_data['human_review'] without a guard: a hand-edited or legacy sidecar missing that key crashes with a raw KeyError traceback instead of a ClickException, and a re-review with no --notes overwrites previously recorded notes with None.

findings.migration: 1) Extract write_human_review and use it in approve_claim; add a missing-key test. 2) Extract the draft-gate predicate from _preflight_status; call it from publish's classification loop. 3) Decide the notes-preservation rule explicitly and test re-review.

findings.title: step-analyze duplicates claim-refresh's claim-context reconstruction (template re-render, entity, sources)

findings.title: pipeline.py is a god-module: three entry points, all step helpers, and a 522-line onboard function in one file
findings.impact: Every pipeline change lands in the #1 hotspot file. onboard_entity alone (ccn_max 73, longest_fn 522 nloc per metrics) mixes entity lifecycle (verifier, enricher, disambiguation), template screening, and per-template claim persistence, so unrelated features collide in the same function and reviews cannot be scoped.

Extract the per-template loop body into a _run_template(cfg, template, resolved_entity, gate) function returning a small outcome enum, shrinking onboard_entity to phase orchestration.

findings.title: Four-branch claim persistence is duplicated between onboard_entity and cli.py claim-refresh, and has already diverged

Divergence already shipped: claim-refresh's blocked sidecars never pass failure=, so pipeline_run.failure triage data (which dr-debug-blocked depends on) is silently dropped on refreshed claims while onboard preserves it.

findings.title: persistence.py's real API is underscore-private and imported function-locally across modules

The underscore names lie about their contract (no deprecation or stability signal), and the function-local import blocks scattered through research_claim/onboard_entity/enrich_entity suggest a circular-import problem that does not exist: pipeline.py already imports orchestrator.persistence at module top.

findings.title: The disambiguation checkpoint is overloaded as a verification-status picker, and auto-approve mode aborts on it
findings.impact: review_entity_disambiguation carries two unrelated decisions: picking among same-name entities, and choosing a verification_status enum for unverified startups. The CLI prompt renders enum values as 'Candidates', which is misleading; free-text answers must be re-validated against the enum in onboard_entity. Because AutoApproveCheckpointHandler returns 'reject' for this method, any unattended onboard of an entity the verifier can't confirm silently dies, which surprises CI/batch operators.
findings.current: onboard_entity passes ['unverified-startup', 'unverified-other'] through the candidates parameter and then pattern-matches the string reply, rejecting out-of-enum free text after the fact.
findings.proposed: Add a dedicated review_verification_status(entity_name, options) -> Literal[...] checkpoint (or a typed ChoiceRequest object on a single gate method) so each decision has its own schema and its own auto-approve policy. Auto mode could then default unverified entities to 'unverified-other' with a warning row instead of aborting, which matches the advisory-not-gate philosophy used elsewhere in onboard.
findings.migration: 1) Add the new protocol method with implementations in both handlers. 2) Switch onboard's unverified branch to it; delete the free-text enum re-validation. 3) Decide the auto-approve default explicitly and document it in AGENTS.md.

findings.title: Claims live in two on-disk layouts (flat for companies/products, typed for subjects)
findings.impact: _claim_dir_for forks on entity type 'for backward compat', so every consumer of research/claims/ (site globs, CLI ref resolvers, review queue, docs) must encode the same fork forever. New entity types silently get the typed layout, widening the split. Ambiguity is latent: a company slugged 'subjects' would collide with the type prefix.
findings.current: Companies and products write research/claims/<slug>/; subjects (and any future type) write research/claims/<type>/<slug>/. The fork lives in persistence but its knowledge is spread across whatever parses claim paths back into entities.
findings.proposed: Migrate to one canonical layout research/claims/{type_dir}/{entity_slug}/ for all types. The site adds redirects from old flat URLs (Astro can emit them from a small mapping), and _claim_dir_for collapses to a single expression.
findings.migration: 1) Script a git mv of company/product claim dirs under companies/ and products/, updating entity refs where paths are stored. 2) Collapse _claim_dir_for and the CLI's _resolve_claim_path. 3) Add site redirects for published claim URLs. 4) Run the linter/citation check over the moved tree.

Site loader walks recursively so it tolerates both, but URL/ref consumers encode the fork.

findings.title: Template screening is an identity stub whose exclusion plumbing never fires
findings.impact: _screen_templates returns every template and an empty exclusion list, yet the excluded-templates concept is plumbed through OnboardResult.templates_excluded, the review_onboard checkpoint signature on all handlers, and the CLI's 'Excluded templates' rendering. Readers and new contributors pay to understand machinery that provably does nothing.

findings.proposed: Either implement the LLM screening the docstring promises, or delete _screen_templates and the excluded plumbing (checkpoint parameter, result field, CLI rendering) until screening is actually scheduled. Deleting is cheaper and reversible; the checkpoint protocol change is mechanical.
findings.migration: 1) Confirm no plan doc schedules LLM screening near-term. 2) Remove the function, the result field, the checkpoint parameter, and CLI rendering in one commit. 3) Re-introduce with a real implementation when scheduled.

verification.note: Stub verified (pipeline.py:1272-1279 ignores entity_description, always returns all/[]). Excluded plumbing spans OnboardResult.templates_excluded, review_onboard on all three handler classes, CLI rendering at cli.py:1668-1671 and checkpoints.py:217-220 — none can ever fire from screening. Docstring marks it MVP, so deletion is safely reversible.

findings.title: Dead imports and mixed dataclass/pydantic field styles in pipeline.py
findings.impact: VerdictAssessment and VOCABULARY_HINT_PREFIX are imported and never used (grep hits only on the import lines), inflating the module's apparent surface. VerificationResult, a Pydantic BaseModel, uses dataclasses.field(default_factory=list) for some fields and pydantic Field(...) for others two lines apart; it works in Pydantic v2 (verified by direct test) but reads as a bug and invites a bad copy-paste into a context where it breaks.
findings.current: Both dataclasses import styles coexist (import dataclasses at line 38, from dataclasses import dataclass, field at line 29), and the BaseModel mixes field() and Field() defaults.
findings.proposed: Delete the two unused imports; standardize VerificationResult on pydantic Field (or plain list defaults via default_factory) so one convention holds per class. A ruff F401/linting gate would prevent recurrence.
findings.migration: 1) Remove unused imports; swap field( for Field( in VerificationResult. 2) Enable ruff F401 in the pipeline lint config if not already on.

findings.title: Two overlapping config knobs: 'tavily' in research_origins is inert, and origin typos vanish silently despite a guard written to prevent exactly that
findings.impact: Operators reading VerifyConfig reasonably conclude research_origins controls which searches run; in reality the web spine is chosen solely by search_backend and _select_research_origins filters research_origins down to ACADEMIC_ORIGINS ({'arxiv'}), so the default 'tavily' entry does nothing. Worse, a typo like 'arxive' is silently filtered out before the 'Unknown academic research origin' warning in execute_searches can fire - that warning is unreachable from the production call path, contradicting its own stated purpose.
findings.current: research_origins defaults to ['tavily', 'arxiv']; the 'tavily' member never reaches any dispatcher. execute_searches carries an else-branch warning for unknown academic origins, but its only production caller passes it a list pre-filtered to ACADEMIC_ORIGINS members, so the branch only runs in tests.
findings.proposed: Split the taxonomy cleanly: search_backend picks the web spine (as today), and a new academic_origins field (default ['arxiv']) lists only academic sources. Validate academic_origins against ACADEMIC_ORIGINS in VerifyConfig.__post_init__ and warn/raise there, so typos fail at construction, not silently mid-run. Delete 'tavily' from the origins default and the now-redundant filter in _select_research_origins.
findings.migration: 1) Add academic_origins to VerifyConfig with __post_init__ validation; keep research_origins temporarily as a deprecated alias feeding it. 2) Simplify _select_research_origins to a topic-gate only. 3) Update research-flow.md's dispatch description and the audit-schema comment. 4) Remove the alias once callers/tests are migrated.

verification.note: Both sides verified: 'tavily' in research_origins reaches no dispatcher (only use filters to ACADEMIC_ORIGINS={'arxiv'}); the unknown-origin warning is unreachable from the sole production caller. findings.title: Backend clients diverge on shared plumbing: duplicated 429 Retry-After parsing, hardcoded timeouts, and no throttle on Brave - the fallback that absorbs burst traffic
findings.impact: Brave is the per-query fallback whenever Tavily is rate-limited or unkeyed - precisely the moment the full query fan-out (up to max_initial_queries concurrent requests) hits it - yet it is the only backend without a proactive token bucket, so it relies on reactive 429 retries that cost up to 30s of wall clock each. Meanwhile the Retry-After parse block is copy-pasted between agent.py and tavily.py, and Brave/Tavily hardcode timeout=15.0 while arxiv.py uses the shared HTTP_READ_S constant whose module promises one tuning point.
findings.current: agent.py and tavily.py each define a 30.0s retry constant and an identical float(header_val)-with-ValueError-fallback block; agent.py registers no throttle bucket; two of three backends bypass common/timeouts.py.
findings.proposed: Add a retry_after_seconds(resp, default) helper next to common/throttle.py and use it in both clients; register a 'brave' token bucket at the plan's documented rate (mirroring the tavily/arxiv pattern) so concurrent fan-out is smoothed before the 429 happens; replace both timeout=15.0 literals with HTTP_READ_S.
findings.migration: 1) Add the helper + a 'brave' bucket registration. 2) Swap both duplicated parse blocks and both hardcoded timeouts. 3) Verify test_brave_search.py/test_tavily_search.py 429 cases still pass; add one test asserting the brave bucket throttles concurrent calls.

verification.note: Verified: identical Retry-After parse blocks; both 15.0 literals equal HTTP_READ_S (unification behavior-free); throttle.py docstring lists Brave among intended buckets but none registered; default fan-out is 7 concurrent queries. Nit: no plan documents a Brave rate; one must be chosen.

findings.title: Scorer failure fails open: the entire unscored candidate pool flows to ingestion, tagged as addressing every sub-question
findings.impact: On a scorer timeout or model error, every raw search candidate - forum posts, off-topic hits, name collisions - is committed with fabricated 'addresses every sub-question' tags. The orchestrator then attempts up to candidate_pool_size (32) fetches and LLM ingests on an unranked list, inflating cost and degrading source quality precisely when the model layer is flaky. The fabricated addresses also pollute the audit sidecar's per-sub-question coverage story, which readers are meant to trust.
findings.current: _fallback_to_candidates returns all candidate URLs with addresses = every sub-question id (or a synthetic 'sq1'), and both scorer exception paths _commit that list. Only downstream blocklist filtering and the pool cap bound it; candidate order is raw search order, not quality order.
findings.proposed: Make the fallback honest and bounded: keep only primary/secondary publisher_quality candidates, cap at max_sources (not pool size), tag addresses as unknown (empty list plus a trace flag like scorer_fallback: true) rather than fabricating full coverage, and let the review_sources checkpoint surface the degraded state to the operator.
findings.migration: 1) Sort/filter the fallback list by publisher_quality and truncate. 2) Add a trace flag and stop fabricating addresses; relax the downstream non-empty-addresses expectation for fallback runs (or use a sentinel id). 3) Update the audit-sidecar writer to render the fallback flag. 4) Extend the scorer-timeout test to assert forum-quality candidates are excluded.

findings.title: Audit sidecar contract is one-sided and silently lossy: pipeline writes research, sub_questions, and pipeline_run.failure; Zod strips all three; no Pydantic model exists on the writer side
findings.impact: The audit trail is the site's core trust feature, yet the site can never render the research trace, sub-questions, or failure diagnostics the pipeline records, and nobody gets an error telling them so. Zod's default strip mode means every future Python-side sidecar addition silently vanishes at build time. The writer (persistence.py) assembles a raw dict with no model, so the only typed contract is the incomplete Zod one.
findings.current: persistence.py writes sidecar keys 'research', 'sub_questions', and 'pipeline_run.failure' that auditSchema in content.config.ts does not declare; z.object() strips them without warning. content-model.md documents only the Zod subset, so the docs match the site's view, not the files on disk.
findings.proposed: Give the sidecar a single owner: a Pydantic Sidecar model in pipeline/common (persistence.py serializes via model_dump). Extend auditSchema to cover every field the model writes, and add a CI check that the two field sets match (the sidecar files themselves are the fixture — validate one against both schemas). Decide explicitly between .strict() (fail on unknown keys, so drift surfaces immediately) or documented passthrough; silent strip is the worst of both.
findings.migration: 1) Define Sidecar/PipelineRun/AuditBlock Pydantic models mirroring the current _write_audit_sidecar dict and switch the writer to model_dump. 2) Add research/sub_questions/failure to auditSchema (optional fields) and mark auditSchema .strict(). 3) Update content-model.md's sidecar table from the model. 4) Add a pipeline test that round-trips a generated sidecar through both schemas.

But data survives on disk, subset rendering is deliberate (the sub-question plan scoped site rendering out; docs match the post-strip view). Drift risk real, reader loss not.
verification.simpler_alternative: Add research/sub_questions/pipeline_run.failure to auditSchema as optional fields and update the content-model.md table; add one pytest asserting the writer's top-level key set. Skip the Pydantic model, .strict(), and CI round-trip machinery.

findings.title: Custom claims loader re-implements glob-loader mechanics and has inconsistent sidecar failure modes
findings.impact: About 75 lines re-implement what Astro's glob loader already does (directory walk, frontmatter parse, digest, render) solely to merge a sidecar file. Worse, failure handling is inconsistent: a sidecar with a YAML syntax error is silently dropped with a console.warn (the claim quietly loses its audit trail, and the digest matches the no-sidecar digest), while a sidecar that parses but violates auditSchema fails the whole build. Both files are pipeline-written; the same defect class gets two opposite outcomes.
findings.current: The loader hand-parses frontmatter with a regex (gray-matter is already a dependency used by scripts/check-citations.ts), walks directories itself, and swallows malformed-sidecar errors. Only one page (the claim detail page) consumes the merged audit field.
findings.proposed: Replace with a standard glob loader for claims plus a second small `audits` collection over 'research/claims/**/*.audit.yaml', joined by id in the claim detail page. That deletes parseMarkdownFrontmatter and walkMdFiles, restores per-file digests/watch behavior, and makes a malformed sidecar a build failure like any other collection entry. If the merge must stay, at minimum make YAML syntax errors fail the build; pipeline-written files should never be malformed silently.
findings.migration: 1) Add an audits collection (glob loader, .audit.yaml pattern, auditSchema). 2) In claims/[...slug].astro, look up the audit entry by claim id. 3) Delete the custom loader and helpers; claims reverts to glob. 4) Confirm the claim page renders identically for claims with and without sidecars.

findings.title: Source classification stores a derivation chain (kind -> source_type -> independence) as three independent fields with no cross-field check
findings.impact: The pipeline derives independence mechanically from source_type (which is itself derived from publisher+kind), then persists all three as if independent. The Zod schema will happily validate a source claiming source_type: primary with independence: independent, a combination the derivation forbids. Readers see contradictory badges; the analyst's verification_level derivation inherits the contradiction. A fourth axis (publisher_quality) exists pipeline-side only, adding vocabulary without adding site meaning.
findings.current: content.config.ts declares kind, source_type, and independence as unrelated optional enums. pipeline/common/source_classification.py maps source_type to independence via a lookup table. The site consumes only independence for the source-quality feature (sourceQuality.ts) and displays kind/source_type as chips.
findings.proposed: Pick one authoritative stored axis per source (independence, since it is what the reader-facing quality logic consumes), keep kind as the format descriptor, and derive source_type at display time or drop it. Where all three must remain during v1, add a superRefine (and matching linter check) enforcing the _INDEPENDENCE_BY_SOURCE_TYPE table so contradictions fail the build instead of rendering.
findings.migration: 1) Add the cross-field consistency check to the sources schema and linter. 2) Audit existing source files against it. 3) Decide source_type's fate at the next schema window; if kept, document it as derived display copy, not an input.

findings.title: Pipeline unit tests never run in CI; regressions can deploy to production untested
findings.impact: Readers and the operator: a pipeline regression (linter, models, orchestrator) can land on main and ride the deploy workflow to production with zero pytest execution. The only test run is the voluntary local `inv check`, and the repo's direct-to-main workflow means the PR trigger rarely fires anyway.
findings.current: ci.yml has exactly two jobs: `check` (npm build + markdownlint + check:citations) and `lint-content` (dr lint). Neither runs pytest. deploy.yml's verify gate reuses ci.yml, so deploys inherit the same gap. Meanwhile tasks.py documents `inv check` as 'Build, lint, and test -- the pre-push gate' and AGENTS.md advertises it the same way, so the documented gate and the enforced gate disagree.
findings.proposed: Add a `test-pipeline` job to ci.yml: setup-uv with cache, `uv sync --dev` in pipeline/, `uv run python -m pytest -m 'not acceptance'`. Acceptance tests stay local (they need live API keys). This closes the gap with one job and makes the verify gate on deploys mean something for the Python half of the repo.
findings.migration: 1. Add test-pipeline job to ci.yml mirroring the lint-content setup steps. 2. Confirm unit tests are hermetic (no API keys) so they pass in Actions. 3. Update ci-deploy.md to document the third job. 4. Optionally fail fast: make deploy's build job need both.

findings.title: Three disagreeing definitions of the quality gate (npm run check, inv check, ci.yml) plus two entry points into the same linter
findings.impact: Anyone changing the gate must edit up to three places, and each currently enforces a different set: npm check = build+md+citations; inv check = that plus pytest; CI = build+md+citations plus dr lint but no pytest. ci-deploy.md claims npm check is the 'full quality gate', which is false relative to both of the others. Separately, `inv audit` invokes the content linter as `python -m linter` while CI invokes it as `dr lint`, so flags and output formats fork.
findings.current: package.json 'check' chains three npm scripts; tasks.py check() calls build+lint+_test_unit; ci.yml re-encodes the steps in YAML and adds dr lint. tasks.py _audit builds a `uv run python -m linter` command line while ci.yml runs `uv run dr lint --format json --severity error`.
findings.proposed: One canonical gate: `inv check` = build + lint:md + dr lint (error severity) + pytest unit. Delete the npm 'check' script (keep the leaf scripts). Have ci.yml install invoke and run `inv check` so CI and local are the same command, keeping only the PR-annotation step as CI-specific sugar around the dr lint JSON output. Standardize on the `dr lint` entry point and retire `python -m linter` from tasks.py.
findings.migration: 1. Extend tasks.py check() to run dr lint --severity error. 2. Point ci.yml at `uv tool install invoke && inv check` (or npx-equivalent) in a single job, or keep two jobs but have each call the inv subtask. 3. Delete package.json 'check'. 4. Rewrite ci-deploy.md's Quality Checks section around the single gate.

evidence.quote: npm run build && npm run lint:md && npm run check:citations
Run full quality gate (same as CI `check` job)
uv run dr lint --format json --severity error > lint-report.json

verification.note: Verified: npm check = build+md+citations; inv check adds pytest; CI adds dr lint but not pytest. Two caveats that soften but don't overturn it: ci-deploy.md:115 scopes 'full quality gate' with '(same as CI check job)', which is accurate as written; and both linter entry points (orchestrator/cli.py:2253 dr lint, linter/__main__.py) share linter.runner.run_all_checks, so only CLI flags/formats fork, not the checks themselves.

findings.title: check-citations.ts duplicates the pipeline linter's broken-source-ref check in a second language

Any schema change (e.g., sources becoming objects) must be fixed twice or the checks silently diverge. The TS version also carries tsx and gray-matter as devDependencies used nowhere else in src/.
findings.current: scripts/check-citations.ts walks research/claims/ and checks source files exist; pipeline/linter/checks.py check_broken_source_refs does the identical check at severity error, and CI already runs it via `dr lint --severity error` in the lint-content job.
findings.proposed: Delete scripts/check-citations.ts, the check:citations npm script, and the tsx + gray-matter devDependencies. Let dr lint be the sole owner of citation integrity (it already is the stricter superset: required fields, unreferenced sources, duplicates).
findings.migration: 1. Confirm lint-content runs on the same triggers as check (it does, same workflow). 2. Remove the script, npm entries, and the two devDependencies. 3. Update ci-deploy.md, research-workflow.md, and site.md references to check:citations. 4. Update tasks.py lint() to drop the npm run check:citations call.

evidence.quote: Verifies that every source slug in a claim's `sources` frontmatter array

verification.note: Verified duplicate: scripts/check-citations.ts and pipeline/linter/checks.py check_broken_source_refs (line 204, severity error) implement the same slug-resolves-to-file rule, and CI runs both in the same workflow (check job via npm, lint-content via dr lint --severity error). Grep confirms tsx and gray-matter are used only by check-citations.ts. Migration correctly covers tasks.py lint() which also calls check:citations.

findings.title: Redirect map maintained in two hand-edited stores that already disagree on trailing slashes
findings.impact: Every route rename needs edits to astro.config.ts (on-site redirect pages) and scripts/seo/redirects.json (Cloudflare edge 301s), plus a manual run of apply-cloudflare-redirects.sh. They have already drifted: the site declares trailingSlash 'never' and astro targets '/research', but every Cloudflare target ends in '/', so edge 301s land visitors and crawlers on non-canonical URLs that the site then treats as duplicates of the canonical slashless form.
findings.current: astro.config.ts hardcodes 13 redirect entries; redirects.json hardcodes 13 near-identical entries with trailing-slash targets; nothing generates one from the other or checks agreement.
findings.proposed: One redirect data module (e.g., src/lib/redirects.ts exporting the map) imported by astro.config.ts, plus a tiny generator that emits redirects.json from it with canonical (slashless) targets. apply-cloudflare-redirects.sh consumes the generated file. Drift becomes impossible and the trailing-slash bug is fixed at the source.
findings.migration: 1. Extract the map to src/lib/redirects.ts; import it in astro.config.ts. 2. Add a 20-line node script to emit redirects.json (slashless targets, subpath variants). 3. Regenerate and re-run apply-cloudflare-redirects.sh once. 4. Add the generator to inv check or a lint step so a stale redirects.json fails.

verification.note: The two-store duplication is real, but the trailing-slash 'drift' is intentional and documented: docs/v1.0.0-roadmap.md:126 and seo-post-restructure.md record that Cloudflare targets ship with trailing slashes to collapse the GH-Pages canonical-slash 301 into a single hop; UNSCHEDULED.md tracks the remaining deep-URL two-hop as known/low priority. The proposed slashless generator would reintroduce the double redirect it was designed to avoid.
verification.simpler_alternative: If drift protection is wanted, a small check script asserting the two maps cover the same source paths is enough; do not force slashless targets.

findings.title: rerun_v1_claims.py is a finished one-shot backfill kept live in scripts/, with the repo's worst function complexity
findings.impact: It reads as active tooling but its job completed 2026-05-05. Its main() has ccn 35 in a 139-line function, it re-implements frontmatter parsing with a regex instead of the pipeline's loaders, and it mutates published claim files via re.subn on `status: draft` - a pattern that will silently no-op or mis-edit if the frontmatter format shifts. If someone runs it today against current content, --force plus that regex rewrite is a data-integrity risk on research/ files.
findings.current: The docstring itself says it is 'Kept around for re-use if a future backfill needs the same preserve-when-unchanged semantics'. It shells out to dr claim-refresh per claim and hand-restores sidecar YAML and status.
findings.proposed: Delete it (git history preserves it) or move it to a clearly-dead archive alongside scripts/llm-tester/archive/. If preserve-sign-off-when-unchanged is genuinely wanted again, it belongs inside the pipeline as a `dr claim-refresh --preserve-unchanged-signoff` flag, where frontmatter round-tripping and sidecar handling already exist and are tested.
findings.migration: 1. Confirm with the operator that the backfill is closed (the rerun log JSONL is the record). 2. git rm the script; note the replacement path in the commit message. 3. If the semantics are still wanted, file the dr flag as pipeline work with tests.

evidence.quote: Kept around for re-use if a future backfill needs the same preserve-when-unchanged

verification.note: Interpretation partly wrong: it does not 'read as active tooling' — the docstring states it is a completed 2026-05-05 backfill kept deliberately for reuse. Accidental-run risk is mitigated: --dry-run exists, claims with verification_level are skipped unless --force, and the status regex only fires when verdict/confidence are unchanged and prior sign-off existed. Complexity (ccn 35 main) is real but frozen. Deleting or archiving is still reasonable housekeeping, at low severity.

findings.title: Graphify graph publish is an unscripted doc-embedded procedure committing a 2.7MB blob into public/
findings.impact: The publish path is copy-paste shell from an architecture doc: cp the generated HTML into public/ and re-inject a noindex meta with an inline python one-liner. Skipping or mistyping the second step ships an indexable 2.7MB page (robots.txt is the only backstop). Each republish also re-commits a multi-megabyte diff, permanently bloating a repo whose research content is already slated to move out for size reasons.
findings.current: docs/architecture/graphify.md instructs: 'cp graphify-out/graph.html public/graphify/graph.html' followed by a python -c snippet, and warns the file 're-commits as a large diff each' republish. graphify-out/ is git-ignored, so public/graphify/graph.html is the only copy under version control.
findings.proposed: A scripts/publish-graphify.sh (or inv graphify.publish task) that does copy + noindex injection + a grep assertion that the meta landed, so the procedure is one command and cannot half-run. Longer term, stop versioning the blob: publish it as a deploy-time step (build job copies graphify-out artifact into dist/) or host it outside the repo, keeping git history lean.
findings.migration: 1. Move the doc's two commands into a script with a post-copy `grep -q 'name="robots"'` check. 2. Replace the doc section with 'run inv graphify.publish'. 3. Decide whether the blob stays in git; if not, add a deploy.yml step that injects it and delete public/graphify/ from the tree.

evidence.quote: The file is 2.6MB and re-commits as a large diff each

verification.note: Facts verified (2.7MB public/graphify/graph.html committed; cp + python one-liner procedure in graphify.md), but impact is overstated: robots.txt Disallow /graphify/ (verified, line 3) already blocks crawling if the noindex step is skipped, and the doc explicitly says to republish deliberately, not per rebuild. 'Slated to move out for size reasons' is not evidenced — graphify.md gives no size rationale for the research/ move. A wrapper script is a nice-to-have.

findings.title: Entity dev-loop scripts hardcode OpenAI/ChatGPT and delete sources by filename glob
findings.impact: Onboarding a different entity for iterate-and-clear testing means copy-pasting new shell files (the pattern already forked once: onboard-openai.sh vs onboard-chatgpt.sh). Worse, clear-openai.sh deletes every research/sources/openai-*.md and chatgpt-*.md by glob without checking whether another entity's claim cites them; a shared source gets deleted and the breakage only surfaces later as a broken-source-ref lint error.
findings.current: Three near-identical scripts: two one-line dr onboard wrappers with hardcoded names/URLs/types, and a clear script with hardcoded entity paths plus a find-glob over sources.
findings.proposed: One parameterized pair: `scripts/onboard-entity.sh <name> <url> <type>` and `scripts/clear-entity.sh <slug>...` where clear consults the citation graph (grep claims' sources: lists, or call dr lint's loader) and refuses to delete sources still cited by out-of-scope claims unless --force. Better still, fold clear into the pipeline as `dr clear <entity>` so slug-to-file mapping stays in one codebase.
findings.migration: 1. Merge the two onboard scripts into one taking args. 2. Rewrite clear to derive source slugs from the deleted claims' frontmatter instead of a filename glob. 3. Delete the three hardcoded scripts.

evidence.quote: uv run dr onboard "OpenAI" https://openai.com --type company --repo-root "$REPO_ROOT"

verification.note: Verified: two hardcoded onboard scripts plus clear-openai.sh deleting sources by find-glob (line 51) with no citation check. One nuance: current pipeline sources are URL-derived slugs under year dirs (research/sources/2026/...), mostly without entity prefixes, so the glob can also miss the entity's own sources and leave orphans — the fragility cuts both ways, which supports the finding's fix (derive slugs from the deleted claims' frontmatter). Low severity is right for dev-only scripts.

findings.title: inspect-urls.sh fetches a fresh gcloud token per URL and hardcodes its URL list in the script body
findings.impact: Each of the 18 inspections spawns `gcloud auth application-default print-access-token` (a slow subprocess), roughly doubling runtime for no benefit since tokens live ~1 hour. The URL list is baked into the script, so inspecting a new page means editing code, even though a sibling data file (request-indexing-queue.txt) shows the list-as-data pattern already exists in the same directory.

findings.evidence_note: 1/2 evidence entries failed grep and were disregarded

verification.note: Verified: inspect_one() runs gcloud auth application-default print-access-token inside the per-URL loop (line 36) for 18 hardcoded URLs (lines 12-31), while sibling request-indexing-queue.txt shows the list-as-data pattern. Hoisting the token and reading URLs from a file is strictly simpler.

findings.title: package.json version 0.1.0 contradicts VERSION.md 1.0.0-beta.2
findings.impact: Two version declarations in the repo disagree; anyone (or any tool) reading package.json concludes the site is pre-alpha while VERSION.md says beta.2. The v1.0.0 rename (from v0.1.0) evidently updated VERSION.md but not package.json.

findings.proposed: Either sync package.json to VERSION.md, or (simpler, since the package is private and never published) delete the version field from package.json and let VERSION.md be the single declaration. If both must exist, add a one-line check to dr lint or inv check that they match.
findings.migration: 1. Pick VERSION.md as canonical. 2. Remove or sync the package.json field. 3. Optional: add the equality check to the gate.

verification.note: Verified both sides: package.json line 4 has "version": "0.1.0"; VERSION.md line 1 reads 1.0.0-beta.2. Package is private and unpublished, so dropping the field or syncing it are both cheap; low severity is right.

findings.title: Every deploy runs the full Astro build twice (verify job builds, build job rebuilds)
findings.impact: Deploy latency and Actions minutes: ci.yml's check job runs npm run build as a smoke test, then deploy.yml's build job checks out and builds again from scratch to produce the artifact. As research/ grows (hundreds of content pages), the doubled build becomes the dominant cost of every push to main.
findings.current: deploy.yml: verify uses ./.github/workflows/ci.yml (whose check job runs npm run build), then a separate build job runs npm ci + npm run build again and uploads dist/.
findings.proposed: Make the built artifact flow through: give ci.yml a workflow_call input (e.g., upload-dist: true) that uploads dist/ from the check job; deploy.yml's deploy step consumes that artifact and the standalone build job disappears. PR runs keep upload-dist false and stay unchanged.
findings.migration: 1. Add the boolean input and conditional upload-pages-artifact step to ci.yml. 2. Delete deploy.yml's build job; point deploy's needs at verify. 3. Verify a manual workflow_dispatch deploy end-to-end.

verification.note: Verified: deploy.yml verify job reuses ci.yml (whose check job runs npm run build), then the build job (needs: verify) checks out and runs npm ci + npm run build again before uploading dist/. The jobs are sequential, so the duplicate build directly adds deploy latency. Proposal is the standard build-once-promote pattern; effort medium is fair given workflow_call input plumbing.

findings.title: CI's Python job bootstraps uv via pip on a pinned 3.12 while local dev runs 3.14
findings.impact: The lint-content job pays setup-python + pip install uv + uncached uv sync on every run, and it lints under Python 3.12 while local development demonstrably runs 3.14 (tasks.py carries a 3.14-specific workaround). Today only dr lint runs there so the skew is mostly latent, but the moment SCI-01 adds pytest to CI, tests would exercise a different interpreter than any developer uses.
findings.current: ci.yml: actions/setup-python with python-version '3.12', then `run: pip install uv`, then uv sync in pipeline/. pipeline/pyproject.toml only requires >=3.12; nothing pins CI to what dev machines run.
findings.proposed: Replace setup-python + pip with astral-sh/setup-uv (built-in uv and dependency caching) and pin the interpreter in one place the tool respects (a .python-version or pyproject requires-python tightened to the actually-used minor), so CI, local, and future test jobs resolve the same Python.
findings.migration: 1. Swap the two steps for astral-sh/setup-uv with enable-cache. 2. Add .python-version (or uv python pin) in pipeline/. 3. Confirm dr lint output unchanged.

verification.note: Verified: ci.yml pins python-version 3.12 and bootstraps uv via pip with no dependency cache; tasks.py lines 60-61 document a Python 3.14 fcntl.ioctl workaround, evidencing 3.14 local dev; pipeline/pyproject.toml only says requires-python >=3.12 and no .python-version exists in pipeline/. Skew is latent today (only dr lint runs in CI), matching the stated low severity.

findings.title: ShouldIDecisionTree is a 947-line hand-rolled client-side SPA rendering build-time-known content via innerHTML
findings.impact: Anyone changing the decision tree must edit HTML-in-template-strings inside a <script> inside a .astro file, with hand-rolled escaping, a hand-rolled step state machine, and ~500 lines of :global() CSS that only exists because the markup is injected at runtime. Readers without JS (and search engines) get an empty card even though every question, answer, and result string is known at build time.
findings.current: The component serializes its data prop to a JSON <script> tag ('const payload = JSON.stringify(data ?? {})'), then a client script JSON.parses it and builds every screen with template literals assigned to content.innerHTML, including its own escape() function. All step styles are declared as .should-i-content :global(...) because Astro's scoper can't see runtime-injected markup.
findings.proposed: Server-render every step (intro, lens, each question, result shell) as hidden sections from the same data at build time; client JS shrinks to visibility toggling plus score accumulation. Extract the scoring/summary logic (generateSummary, generateSuggestions, clamp thresholds) into src/lib/shouldI.ts so it is unit-testable, and let styles become normally scoped.
findings.migration: 1) Move Config types + scoring functions to src/lib/shouldI.ts. 2) Render steps as <section hidden data-step=...> in the component template. 3) Replace render*/innerHTML functions with a show(step) toggle + result fill-in (result numbers via data attrs or small DOM writes). 4) Convert :global() rules to scoped rules and delete escape().

verification.note: Mechanics verified (innerHTML SPA, escape(), 65 :global rules, empty card without JS). But tree content is data-driven from the markdown payload, so content edits never touch template strings; churn is 2 commits on a single leaf page. Real complexity, overstated impact.
verification.simpler_alternative: Server-render only the intro screen (fixes the empty no-JS/SEO card) and move scoring/summary functions to src/lib/shouldI.ts for unit tests; keep the existing client renderer for later steps.

findings.title: SourceRow.astro is dead code, and the chip skin classes it duplicates are declared in five places

VerdictBadge and VerdictDistribution each map verdict names to color tokens independently.

layout can validate its own shape here. Fail loudly: a schema error in a
