findings.title: ResponsibleAIMatrix is the scope's top hotspot because it owns four unrelated concerns, including its child's behavior and a page-level CSS variable contract
findings.impact: 23 commits of churn and hotspot rank 18 (highest in this scope). Any change to filtering, markdown cells, sticky headers, or table layout lands in the same 597-line file. The chip buttons live in ResponsibleAIFilters but their click handling and aria-pressed sync live in the matrix's script, so the two files must be edited in lockstep. The sticky thead silently depends on an IntersectionObserver in resources/[...slug].astro publishing --page-nav-stuck-height.
findings.current: One component holds: (a) renderDetail(), a second implementation of the exact link regex InlineMd already owns; (b) initMatrix(), which drives [data-filter-product] buttons rendered by the child ResponsibleAIFilters; (c) a data-generated '<style is:global set:html=' block emitting one hide-rule per product; (d) a sticky header pinned to a variable set two files away.
findings.proposed: Replace renderDetail with the existing <InlineMd> component (delete the duplicate parser). Move chip click handling + aria-pressed sync into ResponsibleAIFilters so the parent only reads a scoped 'products-changed' event or the data attribute. Replace the generated global stylesheet with the handler toggling hidden on [data-product-key] cells directly, removing string-interpolated CSS. Document the --page-nav-stuck-height contract at both ends (or move the observer into a small PillNav component that owns both sides).
findings.migration: 1) Swap renderDetail calls for <InlineMd text={cell.detail}/>. 2) Move initMatrix's chip logic into ResponsibleAIFilters' own script scoped to its root. 3) Delete the is:global set:html style; toggle hidden per cell in JS. 4) Extract the pill-nav + stuck-height observer into one component used by both the page and TurnOffGuide.

verification.note: Churn (23) and renderDetail/InlineMd regex duplication verified. But the stuck-height contract is documented at both ends (matrix 337, page 105) so not 'silent'; root delegation is a coherent one-owner-of-state pattern; and JS hidden-toggling would break SSR initially-hidden state pre-JS.
verification.simpler_alternative: Replace renderDetail with <InlineMd text={cell.detail}/> at the two cell call sites and delete the duplicate parser; keep the root-scoped delegation and generated hide-rules, which correctly hide initially_hidden products before JS runs.

findings.title: A11yControl and Base.astro's pre-paint script duplicate storage keys and font-size maps by hand, and their motion logic already disagrees
findings.impact: The sync is maintained by a comment ('keep them in sync'), not code. It has already drifted on motion: the pre-paint script sets data-motion purely from localStorage, while A11yControl later ORs in prefers-reduced-motion. A reader with OS-level reduced motion and no stored preference gets data-motion="on" at first paint, so any :root[data-motion="reduce"]-gated CSS animates until the deferred script runs.
findings.current: Base.astro's is:inline script hardcodes 'dr-theme'/'dr-contrast'/'dr-font-size'/'dr-motion' and the px map; A11yControl re-declares them in STORAGE/FONT_SIZE_PX, with the mirroring acknowledged only in comments at both ends.
findings.proposed: One constants module (src/lib/a11yPrefs.ts) exporting keys, the font-size map, and an effectiveMotion(stored, systemReduced) helper. Base's inline script gets the values via define:vars from that import; both scripts compute motion the same way, killing the first-paint gap.
findings.migration: 1) Create src/lib/a11yPrefs.ts with the constants and motion helper. 2) In Base.astro switch to <script is:inline define:vars={...}> fed from the import. 3) Import the same module in A11yControl. 4) Add the matchMedia check to the pre-paint motion computation.

evidence.quote: // Storage keys and font-size values are mirrored in the pre-paint inline

verification.note: Duplication is real and comment-enforced. But the claimed first-paint harm can't occur: every :root[data-motion=reduce] rule is paired with an equivalent prefers-reduced-motion media rule (global.css, resources.css, index.astro, A11yControl), so OS-reduce users see no animation pre-script.

findings.title: .sr-only is defined four times with diverging declarations

verification.note: Four .sr-only declarations verified (global.css:226, Matrix:476, Summary:180, SearchInput:22); the global copy lacks the padding/margin/border resets the matrix copy carries. Low severity is right.

findings.title: Components render class names whose styles live in resources.css, which only ResourcePage loads
findings.impact: TurnOffGuide, ResponsibleAIMatrix, ResponsibleAISummary, and ResponsibleAIFootnotes emit .return-top, .pill-nav-wrap, and .resources-callout markup that is unstyled unless the page happens to use the ResourcePage layout. Reusing any of these components elsewhere (e.g. a research page wanting a return-top button) silently produces broken UI, and nothing in the component files points to where the styles live.
findings.current: resources.css's own header says it is 'Loaded only by ResourcePage.astro and the resources hub', yet four components in src/components/ depend on its rules; the pill-nav markup is additionally duplicated between TurnOffGuide and resources/[...slug].astro.

findings.title: FilterBar/FacetBar/SearchInput are wired through document-global IDs and events, making them undocumented one-per-page singletons
findings.impact: The filter system queries document-wide for #showing-count, #facet-bar, #active-count, .search-input, and every .facet-chip, and communicates via a document-level 'facet-change' event. A second FilterBar on any page cross-wires silently. The same codebase already contains the correct pattern (ResponsibleAIMatrix's initMatrix(root) scopes everything to its root), so the two filter systems follow opposite conventions.
findings.current: FilterBar's define:vars inline script does document.querySelectorAll('[data-filterable]') and getElementById lookups; FacetBar dispatches document.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('facet-change'...)); SearchInput defaults its id to 'search-input'.
findings.proposed: Adopt the initMatrix pattern: FilterBar owns a root element, queries within it (rows live in a sibling container passed by selector or wrapped by the component via slot), and FacetBar dispatches on the FilterBar root instead of document. Delete the id-based coupling.
findings.migration: 1) Give FilterBar a root wrapper and move the row container inside it via a slot (or a data-filter-scope attribute). 2) Rescope all queries/events to that root. 3) Drop fixed ids in favor of root-relative classes. 4) Verify the five index pages still filter.

verification.note: Global IDs/document events verified, and the initMatrix inconsistency is real. But it's latent: each of the five index pages mounts exactly one FilterBar, and rows are DOM siblings by page structure (reason documented in FilterBar's comment), so root-scoping means restructuring all five pages.

findings.title: Topic facet filters only match a claim's first topic, silently hiding multi-topic claims from filtered lists
findings.impact: A reader filtering the claims index by topic B never sees a claim tagged [A, B]; the claim just doesn't appear, which reads as 'no research on this' and undermines the site's completeness promise. The limitation is acknowledged in a code comment but is invisible to readers.
findings.current: ClaimRow emits data-topic={topics[0]} because FilterBar's facet matcher does an exact set-membership test against one attribute value ('values.has(row.getAttribute(...)')).
findings.proposed: Emit all topics space-separated in the data attribute and change the matcher to token intersection (split the attribute, test any overlap). This is a two-line change in each file and removes the known follow-up.
findings.migration: 1) ClaimRow: data-topic={topics.join(' ')}. 2) FilterBar facetMatch: split attribute on whitespace, match if any token is in the selected set. 3) Spot-check a multi-topic claim under each of its topics.

verification.note: Both sides verified: ClaimRow emits only topics[0]; FilterBar's matcher is exact set-membership. Live impact: published claim ai-producers-existential-score (ai-safety + industry-analysis) is invisible under the industry-analysis filter today. Token-intersection fix is safe for the other facets.

findings.title: TreadLightlyAI product names are baked into ResponsibleAIMatrix layout rationale

findings.title: All reader-facing client logic (scoring, markdown parsing, filter matching) is embedded in .astro files with no test harness at all
findings.impact: package.json has no test runner: the decision tree's score-to-verdict thresholds, InlineMd's parser (which feeds set:html-adjacent rendering and the FAQ JSON-LD), and the facet matcher have zero automated coverage. These are exactly the pieces where a silent regression misleads readers (wrong verdict summary, broken links in guide steps, claims missing from filters), and none can even be imported into a test today because they live inside component script blocks.
findings.current: The only checks are 'npm run build', markdownlint, and a citations script ('"check": "npm run build && npm run lint:md && npm run check:citations"'). InlineMd exports parseInline/stripMd from a .astro file; the decision-tree logic is inside an inline <script>; FilterBar's matcher is inside a define:vars script.
findings.proposed: Move pure logic to src/lib/ (inlineMd.ts, shouldI.ts, facetMatch.ts), re-export where components need it, and add vitest with focused unit tests for: parseInline edge cases (nested bold/link/code), stripMd, score clamping/threshold boundaries (35/45/55/65), and multi-value facet matching (pairs with SC-09). Wire 'vitest run' into npm run check.
findings.migration: 1) Add vitest as a devDependency. 2) Extract parseInline/stripMd to src/lib/inlineMd.ts (InlineMd.astro imports it). 3) Extract decision-tree scoring per SC-01 step 1. 4) Write the boundary tests and add to the check script.

verification.note: package.json has no test runner and no JS tests exist (pipeline pytest covers Python only, not client logic). Decision-tree scoring and FilterBar's matcher live in inline scripts that cannot be imported; InlineMd's exports sit in a .astro file needing Astro-aware tooling. Claim holds at medium.

findings.title: Homepage fuses random scatter geometry, glitch engine, and page markup into one 1k-line file with non-reproducible builds
findings.impact: Anyone touching the homepage (30 commits of churn already) navigates ~110 lines of collision geometry, ~530 lines of CSS, and a ~155-line inline animation script in a single file. Worse: card positions come from Math.random() in frontmatter, so they are frozen at build time (every visitor sees the same 'random' layout) and every rebuild produces different HTML — dist diffs are always noisy and visual regression testing is impossible.
findings.current: index.astro computes wedge-polar card positions with rnd()/Math.random(), runs a 12-iteration collision-nudge loop, assigns z-order, and inlines the letter-glitch/dim scheduler as a script — all in the page file.
findings.proposed: Extract the geometry to src/lib/scatter.ts as a pure function taking a seed (derive the seed from the highlighted-claim IDs so output is deterministic per content state and testable with fixed inputs). Move the glitch scheduler to a bundled script file (src/scripts/hero-glitch.ts, loaded via <script src>), and the card markup+styles to a HeroScatter.astro component. index.astro drops to composition plus hero copy.
findings.migration: 1) Move drawPosition/verdictOccluded/z-order into src/lib/scatter.ts with an injectable PRNG (mulberry32-style, seeded); add unit tests for the verdict-occlusion invariant. 2) Extract HeroScatter.astro with the card CSS. 3) Move the inline glitch IIFE to src/scripts/hero-glitch.ts. 4) Verify built HTML is byte-identical across two builds.

evidence.quote: function rnd(min: number, max: number): number {

verification.note: Verified: 1042 lines, 29 commits, Math.random() in frontmatter freezes one layout per build and changes HTML every rebuild; ~155-line inline glitch script. Behavior and metrics check out.
verification.simpler_alternative: Replace rnd()'s Math.random with a ~10-line seeded PRNG (seed from highlighted claim ids) in place. That alone fixes nondeterminism and enables testing; the component/script extraction can be a separate, optional cleanup.

findings.title: Base.astro is head+nav+footer+styles in one hotspot file, and the site ships two independent hamburger-nav implementations
findings.impact: Every nav, footer, SEO, or theme change lands in the same 755-line file (hotspot #9, 40 commits, fan_in 18), so unrelated edits collide. The nav collapse works by cloning the DOM into an offscreen node to measure natural width — fragile JS layout inference. Meanwhile index.astro implements a second, visually-matched burger dropdown with its own Escape/outside-click/aria logic, so any nav behavior fix must be made twice.
findings.current: Base.astro contains the document head, org JSON-LD, a measurement-based collapsing nav (cloneNode + offsetWidth), the footer, the theme boot script, and all their styles. index.astro duplicates the dropdown pattern as hero-burger/hero-nav with parallel open/close/Escape/pointerdown handlers.
findings.proposed: Split Base into Head.astro (meta/OG/JSON-LD/theme boot), SiteNav.astro, and SiteFooter.astro. Give SiteNav a variant prop ('bar' for standard chrome, 'overlay' for the homepage) so one component owns open/close/aria and both call sites share it. Replace the clone-and-measure collapse with a CSS container query or a plain breakpoint — the nav content is static and its natural width is knowable at design time.
findings.migration: 1) Extract SiteFooter and Head (mechanical). 2) Extract SiteNav keeping current behavior; delete the hero-burger script from index.astro and mount SiteNav variant='overlay' there. 3) Replace measureLinks/updateCollapsed with a container-query or fixed breakpoint; keep the ResizeObserver only if measurement proves genuinely necessary. 4) Confirm Base.astro is under ~200 lines.

verification.note: Verified: 755 lines, 40 commits, 17 importers, cloneNode measurement, and a parallel hero-burger with duplicate Escape/pointerdown/aria logic. Caveat: the measurement partly exists because the a11y font-size control (16/18/20px root) changes nav width; a plain px breakpoint would regress that.
verification.simpler_alternative: Extract SiteFooter and Head mechanically, and share one dropdown open/close script between Base's nav and the hero burger. Keep clone-and-measure as-is; it correctly handles the user font-size setting that a fixed breakpoint would not.

findings.title: Site navigation structure is hand-copied in three places and hardcodes the resources list that already lives in a content collection
findings.impact: Adding a resource page or research section requires remembering to edit Base.astro's SECTIONS, research/index.astro's section lists, and (for top-level changes) index.astro's navLinks. A new entry in src/content/resources silently never appears in the nav. The copies have already diverged: Base's Research section omits Subjects/Sources/Criteria while research/index.astro lists them as sections 05-07.
findings.current: Base.astro defines TOP_LINKS and SECTIONS literals (including four hardcoded resource hrefs), index.astro re-declares navLinks, and research/index.astro re-declares primarySections/refSections with its own numbering.
findings.proposed: One src/lib/nav.ts module exporting the IA. Derive the Resources links from getCollection('resources') (title + id already exist there) and keep research sections as a single exported list that both Base's nav and the research hub's numbered index render from.
findings.migration: 1) Create src/lib/nav.ts with SECTIONS; derive resources entries from the collection in Base's frontmatter. 2) Point research/index.astro's section lists at the same export. 3) Delete index.astro's navLinks in favor of the shared TOP_LINKS.

verification.note: Triple maintenance is real, but the cited 'divergence' is deliberate curation: Base's Research links mirror research/index's primarySections (+Values); 05-07 are that page's own reference tier. Deriving nav from the resources collection also needs per-entry nav labels (collection titles like 'The Bad News: FLI's latest AI Safety Index' don't fit a nav), so the proposal partly moves complexity.

findings.title: Companies, products, and subjects index pages are three copies of the same page
findings.impact: The card-building frontmatter, grid markup, and grid CSS are byte-similar across three files. findings.proposed: One EntityIndexGrid.astro component taking entityType, title, and a showFilter flag; the three route files shrink to a title plus one component call. (Keeping three physical routes is fine — Astro's file routing wants them — but they should contain no logic.)
findings.migration: 1) Extract the frontmatter card-building into the component (or a lib function). 2) Replace the three page bodies with the component. 3) Decide deliberately whether subjects gets the FilterBar; today's difference looks accidental.

The claim detail page even defines a local isoDate() helper eight lines after hand-inlining the identical logic for asOfDate — a reader can't tell if the two are meant to differ.

findings.migration: 1) Add src/lib/dates.ts with isoDate handling Date | string | null. 2) Replace the five-plus call sites via grep for "instanceof Date". 3) Delete the local helper in claims/[...slug].astro.

findings.title: FAQ exists twice on /research and the JSON-LD copy has already drifted into overstating human review
findings.impact: Reader trust and honesty are this site's product. The visible FAQ carefully says every published claim 'aspires to be reviewed' by a human, but the hand-maintained FAQPage JSON-LD tells search engines every claim 'is reviewed and approved by a human operator' — a stronger guarantee than the site makes to people reading it. Search snippets and AI answer engines will quote the structured data. Every future FAQ edit risks the same silent divergence because the answers are maintained in two formats in one 650-line file.
findings.current: research/index.astro contains a ~70-line faqSchema object with condensed answer strings, followed by the same eight questions as <details> HTML. Nothing ties the two together.
findings.proposed: A single faq data structure (array of { question, answerHtml }) in the frontmatter or src/lib/faq.ts; render the <details> list from it and derive the JSON-LD text by stripping tags from answerHtml. One edit point, impossible to drift.
findings.migration: 1) Move the visible answers into a data array (keep HTML strings, render with set:html). 2) Generate faqSchema from that array (strip tags for the 'text' field). 3) Diff old vs new JSON-LD output once, correcting the 'is reviewed' overstatement to match the visible hedge.

evidence.quote: Every published claim is reviewed and approved by a human operator before appearing on the site.
claim aspires to be reviewed and approved by a human operator

verification.note: Both strings verified. JSON-LD asserts unconditional human review while the visible FAQ says 'aspires' and claim pages ship 'Unreviewed' badges, so the structured data overstates. Note the visible methodology section also says 'Nothing is published without human sign-off' - align that in the same pass.
verification.simpler_alternative: One-line edit: change the JSON-LD answer text to the hedged wording today. The single-source faq array is the durable fix but is not required to stop the live overstatement.

findings.title: The footer's Methodology link lands on a collapsed accordion
findings.impact: Every page's footer links to /research#methodology, but the target is a closed <details> element. The browser scrolls to a shut summary row and the methodology text — the site's core credibility content — stays hidden. Readers who click 'Methodology' see an FAQ list, not the methodology.
findings.current: Base.astro's footer links to /research#methodology; research/index.astro gives the methodology <details> that id but has no script to open it on hash navigation.
findings.proposed: Either promote the methodology to always-visible content (its importance argues for its own section or page), or add a small inline script on /research that opens the matching <details> when location.hash targets one (and on hashchange).
findings.migration: 1) Decide: dedicated methodology section vs auto-open script. 2) If script: on DOMContentLoaded and hashchange, document.querySelector(location.hash)?.closest('details')?.setAttribute('open',''). 3) Re-test the footer link and the deep link from claim pages.

verification.note: Verified: footer links /research#methodology on every page; the id is on a closed <details> and no script opens it. Browsers' ancestor-details reveal only opens details ANCESTORS of a fragment target, not a details that is itself the target, so it stays shut. Reader sees only the collapsed summary row.

findings.title: Homepage injects claim titles into HTML unescaped via regex bolding and set:html
findings.impact: boldInTitle() wraps entity names and vocabulary terms in <strong> tags on the raw title string and the result is rendered with set:html. Claim titles are authored by the LLM pipeline and merged via research-content PRs; any title containing <, >, or & renders broken markup on the homepage, and a malicious or careless title is a stored-XSS path on the highest-traffic page. Astro's default escaping is being deliberately bypassed with no sanitization step.
findings.current: index.astro builds titleHtml by regex-replacing terms with $1 on the unescaped title and passes it to .
findings.proposed: HTML-escape the title first, then apply the bolding regexes to the escaped string (the search terms are plain words, so escaping does not break matching); or replace regex bolding with a token-split render that emits <strong> elements from the template so no set:html is needed.
findings.migration: 1) Add an escapeHtml helper (or use a tiny known-good one) in the same lib as the extracted scatter code. 2) Escape before boldInTitle's replaces. 3) Add a test with a hostile title fixture ('').

verification.note: Verified: raw claim title -> regex <strong> wrapping -> set:html with no escaping. Titles with &, <, > break markup; hostile title is stored XSS. Build-time and pipeline/human-reviewed content keeps this at medium as stated. Minor: terms containing & need escaping too before matching the escaped title.

findings.title: Matrix 'last updated' shells out to git at build time and reports wrong dates on CI shallow clones
findings.impact: resources/[...slug].astro runs execSync('git log -1 …') to caption the Responsible AI matrix with a last-updated date. The deploy workflow uses actions/checkout with the default shallow depth, where the single boundary commit appears to have touched every file — so the caption likely shows the latest deploy date for content that hasn't changed, silently inflating freshness. The pubDate fallback only fires when git throws, not when it returns a misleading date, so the failure is invisible.
findings.current: Per matrix entry, the page shells out to git for the file's last commit date; catch falls back to pubDate only on subprocess error.
findings.proposed: Make freshness an explicit frontmatter field (updatedDate) on the resource entry, maintained where the content is edited — the pipeline and PR review already govern these files. Drop the git subprocess entirely; if a git-derived date is ever wanted, set fetch-depth: 0 in deploy.yml and verify the boundary-commit case in CI.
findings.migration: 1) Add optional updatedDate to the resources collection schema. 2) Caption from updatedDate ?? pubDate. 3) Delete the execSync block and the node:child_process import.

verification.note: Verified: execSync git log per matrix entry; deploy.yml uses actions/checkout default depth 1, where the boundary commit has no parent so `git log -1 -- file` returns HEAD's date for every file. Caption shows latest-deploy date; catch only fires on subprocess error, so the wrong date is silent.

findings.title: Homepage advertises a ?q= search endpoint that the claims page ignores
findings.impact: The WebSite JSON-LD SearchAction tells Google the site supports /research/claims?q={term} (this is what powers sitelinks search boxes). FilterBar's script initializes its query to an empty string and never reads location.search, so a user arriving via that URL gets the full unfiltered list — the advertised capability doesn't exist.
findings.current: index.astro emits a SearchAction with urlTemplate .../research/claims?q={search_term_string}; FilterBar.astro's inline script starts with textQuery = '' and only updates it from input events.
findings.proposed: Smallest honest fix: initialize FilterBar from new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('q'), populate the search input, and call applyFilters() once on load. Alternatively delete the SearchAction until search-by-URL is real; advertising unimplemented behavior in structured data is the same class of drift as SP-06.
findings.migration: 1) In FilterBar's script, read q on init, set the input value, run applyFilters(). 2) Optionally sync input changes back to the URL with replaceState. 3) Manually verify /research/claims?q=water filters on load.

verification.note: Both sides verified: SearchAction advertises /research/claims?q={term}, and no file in src reads location.search or URLSearchParams anywhere, so the parameter is dead. Claims index does use FilterBar with data-title search, so the init-from-URL fix is small and honest.

findings.title: Claim pages render raw source slugs as the visible Sources list even though source titles are already loaded
findings.impact: The 'Sources' section a reader sees on every claim page prints IDs like '2025/colt-dcs-sustainability-report…' as link text, while the collapsed audit-trail section on the same page already resolves the same IDs to human titles via sourceMap. Readers get the worst presentation of the site's most trust-critical data, and a dangling source ref silently becomes a 404 link.
findings.current: claims/[...slug].astro maps claim.data.sources to {sourceRef}; the sourceMap Map built a few lines earlier is used only in the audit trail.
findings.proposed: Look each sourceRef up in sourceMap and render title + publisher (reuse the audit trail's row treatment or SourceRow.astro); fail the build (or at least log loudly) when a ref has no matching source entry instead of emitting a dead link.
findings.migration: 1) Replace the anchor body with sourceMap.get(sourceRef)?.data.title ?? sourceRef. 2) Add publisher/kind meta to match the audit list. 3) Add a build-time warning for unresolved refs.

verification.note: Verified: visible Sources list renders raw refs as link text (line 244) while sourceMap (line 77) resolves the same ids to titles for the audit trail. Minor inaccuracy: sourceMap is also used for source counts, not only the audit trail; immaterial to the finding.

findings.title: Criteria SEO-title normalizer deletes legitimate all-caps words and slices titles mid-word
findings.impact: normCriteriaText strips any whitespace-delimited [A-Z_]+ token to clean up unreplaced placeholders — but that also deletes real acronyms like ' AI ', ' GPU ', or ' LLM ' from criterion text, producing subtly corrupted <title> tags and meta descriptions on criteria pages (e.g. 'discloses AI energy usage' becomes 'discloses energy usage'). The hard .slice(0, 42) then truncates mid-word. These are exactly the pages meant to earn search traffic.
findings.current: criteria/[slug].astro replaces the first COMPANY/PRODUCT occurrence, then regex-deletes every standalone all-caps token, then slices the page title to 42 characters.
findings.proposed: Restrict the cleanup to the known placeholder vocabulary (COMPANY|PRODUCT|ENTITY) instead of all caps tokens, use replaceAll for the substitutions, and truncate at a word boundary with an ellipsis. Better: have the pipeline emit a display_text or seo_title per criterion so the site stops guessing.
findings.migration: 1) Change the regex to /\b(COMPANY|PRODUCT|ENTITY)\b/g and use replaceAll. 2) Word-boundary truncation helper shared with other title slicing (.slice(0,155) descriptions have the same issue). 3) Spot-check generated titles for criteria containing 'AI'.

verification.note: Verified against real criterion texts: 'COMPANY contributes to AI safety causes' becomes 'AI Company contributes to safety causes' (the \s+[A-Z_]+\s+ regex eats ' AI '), and 'score D or worse' loses ' D '. slice(0,42) truncates mid-word. Low severity as stated.

findings.title: One concept, five names: Category (py) / Category (ts) / topics (schema) / topic (URL, CLI) / category (CSS)
findings.summary: The claim-classification vocabulary is named Category in both code layers but topics/topic everywhere a human or LLM touches it, and the site keeps three hand-synced copies of the value list in one file plus a fourth in research.ts.
findings.failure_scenario: A contributor adding a ninth topic must find and edit the Python Category enum, the TS Category type, CATEGORY_LABELS, and three separate z.enum lists in content.config.ts; missing any one produces build-time rejection of valid pipeline output or a topic page that 404s.

evidence.quote: @click.option("--topic", default=None, help="Audit all claims with a given topic")

findings.recommendation: Canonical term: topic. Rename both Category types to Topic and CATEGORY_LABELS to TOPIC_LABELS; collapse the three z.enum copies in content.config.ts to one shared const.

verification.note: Verified: Category enum (models.py:112), Category type+CATEGORY_LABELS (research.ts:1-22), two 8-value z.enum copies in content.config.ts (154,256), category CSS class (ClaimRow.astro:36). getStaticPaths in [topic].astro:11 uses CATEGORIES, so a value present in Python/Zod but missing from research.ts really does 404 the topic page. One inaccuracy: 'three hand-synced copies... in one file' overcounts — content.config.ts has 2 exact copies (claims+criteria); the 'third' (resources, line 410) is a different vocabulary, already covered separately by TAXD-02.
verification.simpler_alternative: A CI check asserting Python Category values == content.config.ts topics enum == research.ts CATEGORIES would eliminate the build-break/404 failure mode without a cross-language identifier rename; cheaper than renaming, though it doesn't resolve the grep-ability confusion.

findings.title: Field name `topics` is reused by the resources collection with an incompatible vocabulary
findings.summary: claims/criteria `topics` draws from the 8-value Category vocabulary; resources `topics` is a different 4-value enum including 'responsible-ai', which is not a Category. Same field name, two value sets, one schema file.
findings.failure_scenario: A contributor who greps 'topics' or copies the claims enum into the resources collection (or vice versa) silently changes which frontmatter validates; 'responsible-ai' on a claim fails the build while looking exactly like a legal topic elsewhere in the same file.
findings.recommendation: Either fold resource topics into the main vocabulary (add responsible-ai as a Category) or rename the resources field to something honest like `themes` so one word maps to one vocabulary.

verification.note: Verified: content.config.ts:154 (claims topics, 8-value) vs :409-411 (resources topics, 4-value incl. 'responsible-ai', not a Category value). Same field name, incompatible enums, in the same file. Evidence and mismatch both check out as described.

findings.title: `verdict` has three meanings; AnalystOutput.verdict holds an object whose .title is the claim title
findings.summary: verdict = the 7-value enum (schema), the analyst's whole output model (AnalystOutput.verdict: VerdictAssessment, which contains title, narrative, topics, seo_title), and per AGENTS.md 'the combined post-review artifact'. Code like ao.verdict.title reads as nonsense until you learn the local dialect.
findings.failure_scenario: A contributor asked to 'log the verdict' at a pipeline call site can plausibly serialize the entire VerdictAssessment (leaking prompt-sized narrative into logs) or the enum, and both type-check paths exist within two attribute hops.

evidence.quote: The combined post-review artifact is the **verdict**.

findings.recommendation: Reserve `verdict` for the enum value. Rename VerdictAssessment -> ClaimAssessment and AnalystOutput.verdict -> assessment. Python-only change; persistence.verdict_write_kwargs and pipeline.py import line 43 are the main touch points.

verification.note: Verified: VerdictAssessment (agent.py:137) holds title/narrative/topics/seo_title/takeaway plus verdict; AnalystOutput.verdict: VerdictAssessment (agent.py:220). ao.verdict.title is legal Python. AGENTS.md:11 defines a third 'verdict' meaning exactly as quoted.

findings.title: `verdict_only_agent` is misleadingly named: it produces the full VerdictAssessment, not only a verdict
