clean_slates.title: One agent runtime, three declarative roles
clean_slates.summary: Rebuild the trio as three declarative role definitions (instructions + typed output model + typed prompt renderer) executed by a single shared runner that owns model resolution, timeouts, null-body retry, and post-run validation. The orchestrator and CLI become thin callers of the same three entry points, and the source contract between roles is one typed packet.
clean_slates.design: A pipeline/roles/ package with one folder per role (ingestor/, analyst/, auditor/), each exporting exactly three things: INSTRUCTIONS (instructions.md plus declared common fragments), OutputModel (Pydantic, with field validators), and render_prompt(input) where input is a typed model (IngestRequest, AnalysisRequest, AuditRequest) built on a shared common.SourcePacket carrying title/publisher/summary/quotes/body plus classifier-stamped kind/independence/source_id. One runner, run_role(role, request, *, model, timeout_s, deps=None), owns resolve_model, per-run model passing (no module singletons, no 'test' placeholder, no override dance), the Infomaniak null-body retry, and a per-role post_validate hook (the ingestor's semantic checks, including the key-quote check fed by the fetch's page text, run here on every path). Tools stay ingestor-local and register on an agent constructed inside the runner. The auditor is named auditor everywhere including docs; its bundle carries the real claim_id and the same SourcePacket the analyst saw, minus verdict/confidence/title. A build-time check asserts every enum literal named in any instructions.md exists in common.models, killing the topic/subject and missing-paper class of drift. CLI step commands and the orchestrator both call run_role, so timeout, retry, slug, and validation behavior cannot fork.
clean_slates.tradeoffs: More indirection for a three-agent system: a contributor can no longer read one file and see everything an agent does, and the runner accumulates conditional handling (only the ingestor needs deps/tools, only the analyst has a second verdict-only output form) that generic code expresses less clearly than today's explicit call sites. Per-role post-validation hooks in a registry are less discoverable than inline field_validators. The migration itself touches every orchestrator call site and the tests that monkeypatch module-level agents, and renaming persisted vocabulary (if the auditor/evaluator decision goes the other way) forces a sidecar schema_version bump. Per-run model passing gives up the small connection-reuse benefit the cached resolve_model + long-lived singleton combination currently gets for free, so the runner must keep the lru_cache on resolve_model to avoid leaking httpx clients.
dependencies: pydantic-ai (Agent.run(model=...), output_type, tools, TestModel for tests)

stress_test.dependency_check: All deps already present & used exactly as assumed: pydantic-ai 1.84.1 (Agent.override, TestModel, output_type, tools), pydantic v2, httpx, bs4 all in pipeline/pyproject.toml. Confirmed Agent.run() already accepts model= directly, so the 'no override dance' claim is achievable with existing API today, not speculative.
stress_test.migration_cost: Honest that it touches every orchestrator call site + tests, but understates scope: 4 more agents outside the trio (researcher's url_scorer/planner/enricher/verifier) use the identical module-singleton+.override pattern and are left out, leaving two coexisting invocation idioms. pipeline.py(2178L)/cli.py(2340L) need rewrites; 9+ test files rewrite .override(TestModel) sites.
stress_test.simpler_alternative: Skip the roles/ package and runner abstraction. Just: (1) route cli.py's step-ingest through the same _ingest_one/_run_with_null_retry path pipeline.py already has (fixes the missing validate_source_file call + hardcoded 120s timeout I found), (2) replace Agent('test',...).override(model=) with direct .run(prompt, model=resolve_model(...)), which pydantic-ai already supports per-call.
stress_test.note: Confirmed real bug the design would fix: pipeline.py's _ingest_one never calls validate_source_file (only cli.py step-ingest does), and uses cfg.ingest_timeout_s vs a hardcoded 120s in cli.py -- exactly the 'timeout/retry/validation can fork' problem it cites. Tradeoffs section is unusually candid about its own added indirection.

clean_slates.title: common/ rebuilt as vocabulary, content I/O, and runtime — with the vocabulary as checked data
clean_slates.summary: Rebuild the shared package as three explicit layers instead of fourteen sibling files: a vocabulary layer whose values are data with a drift check against the site schema, a content I/O layer with symmetric read/write pairs and one path authority, and a runtime layer for providers/throttle/timeouts/logging. The dumping-ground question resolves itself because every module must name its layer.
clean_slates.design: (1) common/vocab: enums, topic list, publisher tiers, tracking params, and the blocklist all defined in research/*.yaml (extending the existing blocklist.yaml precedent), loaded into typed Python objects at import, with a pytest drift-guard comparing enum value sets against src/content.config.ts (regex extraction, no TS toolchain). (2) common/content: paths.py (repo root + every research/ path), frontmatter.py (parse/serialize with the custom dumper), sidecar.py (read AND write, corruption surfaced as a warning + sentinel), loader.py. (3) common/runtime: providers.py (resolve_model with per-agent DEFAULT_MODELS, tier caps, one shared httpx.AsyncClient per base URL), throttle.py unchanged (it is already the best-designed module in the package), timeouts.py, logging.py (handlers/run-id only), console.py (glyphs/progress/hr owned by the CLI-facing side). templates.py joins content/ with a single tokenizer feeding render, blocked-title render, and title validation.
clean_slates.tradeoffs: Moving vocabularies to YAML makes 'grep the enum' a two-hop lookup and adds load-time failure modes where import-time NameErrors used to be; contributors editing research/ data can now change classification behavior without a code review gate, which needs a CI check to compensate. The three-layer split re-touches all ~48 importers of common.models, a mechanical but noisy migration, and re-export shims linger for a release. Per-base-URL shared HTTP clients introduce lifecycle management (who closes them) that today's leak-but-short-lived CLI process simply ignores. Total file count in common/ goes up, not down.

stress_test.dependency_check: PyYAML/pydantic/pydantic-ai/httpx/click/pytest already in pyproject.toml, used this way today (blocklist.py's lru_cache YAML loader, models.py's OpenAIProvider/FallbackModel). No new library risk. Regex Zod-extraction proven for one field only (test_entity_resolution.py); enum-to-YAML with dynamic Enum construction is unproven at 11-enum scale, untested for pydantic-ai schema gen.
stress_test.migration_cost: Layer split (paths.py, sidecar write, console split, tokenizer) matches findings' step-by-step migrations with shims. Understated: resolve_repo_root() shells to git via subprocess; moving core enums to YAML makes every import-time enum use (~35+ files incl. LLM output schemas) depend on git+filesystem+YAML parse, where today it's zero-I/O. A broken checkout now breaks agent calls, not just CLI startup.
stress_test.simpler_alternative: Keep the three-layer split, path authority (CMN-07), symmetric sidecar (CMN-05), console/logging split (CMN-06), template tokenizer (CMN-09) - each independently justified. Skip YAML-ifying the 11 core enums: ship CMN-02's regex drift-guard test instead; move only operator-edited data (publisher tiers CMN-04, topic validation CMN-03) to YAML, matching blocklist.yaml.
stress_test.note: Design is self-aware (admits load-time failure modes, unresolved AsyncClient lifecycle) but vocab-as-YAML goes beyond any single finding - CMN-02 asked for a drift test, not a data migration - and relocates a zero-churn, zero-I/O module's risk into git/filesystem/YAML failure for the highest-fan-in code. Rest of the split (content/runtime) is sound.

clean_slates.title: Three-tier docs: generated reference, one narrative doc per subsystem, lint-enforced work tracking
clean_slates.summary: Rebuild the docs subsystem around a hard split between facts the code can emit, narratives only humans can write, and work-tracking state a linter can police. Every fact lives in exactly one file; everything else links.
clean_slates.design: Tier 1, generated reference (docs/reference/): a small script (invoked as `dr docs` or `inv docs`) introspects the click CLI (main.commands), VerifyConfig dataclass fields, the CheckpointHandler protocol, and the Zod schema to emit the CLI table, config-knob table, checkpoint list, and content-model field tables as Markdown. CI regenerates and diffs; drift fails the build, which retires the whole DOCS-01 class permanently. Tier 2, narrative (docs/architecture/): exactly one hand-written doc per subsystem — workflow (research-workflow absorbs research-flow's diagrams), onboarding, source-quality, site, ci-deploy, plus glossary as the single vocabulary/cross-walk owner and vision-state-machine as the one flagged aspiration doc. Role definitions exist once (glossary cross-walk); AGENTS.md shrinks to the contract: rules, boundaries, lifecycle, and links. Tier 3, work tracking: UNSCHEDULED.md plus docs/plans/ with a machine-readable status header (draft | ready | in-progress | shipped-tail | done); a dr lint docs check enforces: no 'done'/'shipped-tail' plan outside completed/, no committed doc linking a gitignored path, every plan has a Review history, every architecture doc is listed in README.md. completed/ moves to docs/history/ with a disclaimer README and is excluded from graphify and default doc search.
clean_slates.tradeoffs: The doc generator is new code with its own tests and becomes a build dependency; generated tables read drier than curated prose and lose hand-written 'Notes' columns unless the script supports annotation merge. One-doc-per-subsystem makes research-workflow.md long (~400 lines with diagrams inline). The link/status linter adds CI time and will produce friction on quick doc edits. Moving completed/ to docs/history/ breaks dozens of existing inbound links in one large rename commit, and excluding history from graphify makes past design rationale harder to discover from graph queries — you trade retrieval convenience for answer accuracy.
dependencies: tsx + gray-matter (already dev dependencies, for the link/status checks over Markdown)
existing pipeline/linter/ dr lint framework for the docs checks

stress_test.dependency_check: click, dataclasses.fields, CheckpointHandler Protocol, tsx+gray-matter, markdownlint-cli2, pipeline/linter/ all verified present. But content-model table needs Zod introspection from src/content.config.ts (TypeScript) -- a Python click-based 'small script' can't do that; it's really two generators (Python + tsx) with two CI diff steps, not one.
stress_test.migration_cost: Understates two costs it names in its own tradeoffs: annotation-merge (generated tables losing hand-written Notes) is unsolved, and status-header retrofit onto docs/plans hits real inconsistency -- only 10/21 active plans have any frontmatter, rest use free-text '**Status**:' lines, so 'draft|ready|shipped-tail|done' enum requires touching ~70 files incl. archive. completed/->docs/history/ rename cost is honestly stated. Graphify exclusion is cheaper than implied: .graphifyignore already exists and works; adding completed/ is a one-line change, not new machinery.
stress_test.simpler_alternative: Scope the generator to the CLI table only (DOCS-01: proven drift, high churn) and skip auto-generating config/checkpoint/content-model tables. Do Tier 2 consolidation now (merge research-flow into research-workflow, single glossary role table) -- zero new deps, kills DOCS-04/DOCS-08 duplication directly. Replace the enforced status-enum with DOCS-07's own proposal: one lifecycle rule plus UNSCHEDULED rows, no schema retrofit.
stress_test.note: Findings DOCS-01 through DOCS-12 are well-evidenced and the three-tier framing (generated/narrative/tracked) is directionally right. But the clean_slate oversells the generator as a single small script that 'retires the whole DOCS-01 class permanently' across four heterogeneous sources, and the tradeoffs section already contains the disqualifying admissions (annotation-merge, doc length growth) without pricing them into migration_cost. Tier 2 prose consolidation is the real 80% win and should ship independent of Tier 1/3.

clean_slates.title: Schema-first linter: one Pydantic model layer, a scoped check registry, one CLI
clean_slates.summary: Structural validation stops being hand-copied string sets and becomes Pydantic models shared with the rest of the pipeline; only referential and policy checks remain bespoke, registered with explicit scopes. One CLI serves every entry point, and a CI drift check keeps the Python models honest against the Zod schemas.
clean_slates.design: (1) ClaimFrontmatter / EntityFrontmatter / SourceFrontmatter Pydantic models (extra='forbid') live in pipeline/common/models.py, built from the enums already there; lint pass 1 validates every file against its model, turning parse failures and ValidationErrors into first-class issues (unparseable-frontmatter, invalid-value, unknown-key, missing-field). (2) Cross-file and policy checks (orphaned refs, duplicate slugs, sign-off, cap rules, staleness) register via @check(id, severity, scope='file'|'corpus') into a CHECKS list; the runner builds one LintContext (frontmatter maps, entity/source indexes, template slugs, sidecars, today) and loops the registry, skipping corpus-scope checks when --entity is set. (3) dr lint is the only CLI (click); python -m linter delegates to it and inv audit shells to it; root always resolves via git rev-parse and a 0-files run exits nonzero. prune becomes `dr prune-sources`, reusing the corpus index instead of running all checks to harvest one. (4) enum_drift.py grows a key-set comparison between the Pydantic models and src/content.config.ts and runs in CI, so the two schema layers (Python authoring-time, Zod build-time) are allowed to exist but never to diverge silently.
clean_slates.tradeoffs: Two schema definitions still exist — Python cannot execute Zod — so correctness now depends on the CI drift check being maintained. Pydantic ValidationError messages are blunter than today's hand-written per-check hints; recovering hint quality needs a small error-to-hint translation table, which partially recreates the prose being deleted. The registry adds indirection: you can no longer read one check function and see exactly when and with what inputs it runs. Migration touches every check signature at once, a diff that is mechanically simple but noisy to review.

stress_test.dependency_check: pydantic>=2.0, click>=8.1, pyyaml>=6.0 are all already in pipeline/pyproject.toml, no new deps needed; extra='forbid'/enum/date validation are real Pydantic v2 features. But the design leans on 'existing' enum_drift.py CI tooling that is not a dependency here at all -- it's an unwired one-off script (see migration_cost).
stress_test.migration_cost: CLI merge (item 3) is honestly scoped: __main__.py and dr lint already call the same runner/report functions; tasks.py swap is mechanical. Item 4 overstates enum_drift.py: it's an unwired one-off script (docs/reports/.../scripts/) that only diffs enum VALUES via regex+Jaccard, not object keys. Real field-name drift CI is uncosted net-new work, not a 'grow'.
stress_test.simpler_alternative: Skip the registry/decorator/LintContext rewrite: LINT-02's own migration notes show the actual fix is a one-line entity_filter guard, not new architecture. Ship just the 3 Pydantic models (kills LINT-01/07/09) + that one-line guard + the CLI merge. Add a plain (fn,id,severity,scope) list if scope filtering is ever needed -- skip decorators.
stress_test.note: Direction is sound (real duplicate-schema pain, no dependency gaps) but two corrections needed: enum_drift.py is described as existing CI infra to extend when it's actually an unwired one-off script that only diffs enum values, not object keys -- building real key-drift detection is uncosted; and the check-registry layer adds indirection the design's own tradeoffs section admits, for a problem (LINT-02) whose real fix is a one-line guard per the plan's own migration notes.

clean_slates.editorial_note: Editorial correction: this design's reference to "enum_drift.py" points at a one-off script written for THIS analysis (docs/reports/codebase-analysis-2026-07/scripts/), not an existing pipeline tool. The analyst found it while reading the repo and assumed prior art. The stress-test skeptic caught this (see dependency_check); treat any 'grows enum_drift.py' language in the design text as 'build an enum-drift CI check from scratch', not 'extend existing tooling'.

clean_slates.title: dr as a thin command shell over one persistence service
clean_slates.summary: Rebuilt today, the CLI would be a commands/ package where every command is under ~50 lines: parse arguments, call exactly one library function, render its returned result. All claim-writing branch logic would live in a single persist_verify_outcome service in persistence.py, and all controlled vocabularies would be imported from common.models only.
clean_slates.design: pipeline/orchestrator/cli.py keeps the click group, _CategorizedGroup, and a shared @pipeline_options decorator + build_verify_config helper. commands/steps.py holds step-research/ingest/analyze/audit (read-only by default, --write opt-in, sharing a load_claim_context loader). commands/pipeline.py holds onboard, claim-probe, claim-draft, claim-refresh, entity-enrich; claim-refresh becomes ~60 lines because persist_verify_outcome(vr, ..., reset_review=True) owns the blocked/failed/bad-title/success branches for both it and onboard_entity, always recording failure diagnostics. commands/curation.py holds review, publish, review-queue, lint, stats; publish and review share one gate predicate and one write_human_review helper so 'publishable' is defined once. review_queue.py and stats.py stay as-is structurally but derive their vocabularies (_ALLOWED_VERDICTS, ACQUISITION_ORIGINS) from common.models enums so the existing enum-drift checker covers them. Rendering (the hr()/echo report blocks) moves to a small render.py so command bodies stay declarative. Provider preflight keys off resolve_model's own provider parsing rather than a parallel prefix table, eliminating the 'test' substring sentinel.
clean_slates.tradeoffs: More files and one more level of indirection for a solo-maintainer project where cmd-F in one file currently finds everything. The shared persist function needs a carefully shaped parameter object or it degenerates into a kwargs blob serving two callers. Deferred per-command imports become module-level imports in command modules, which is cleaner but means `dr --help` imports slightly more unless click lazy-loading is added (more ceremony). The migration itself churns the repo's #2 hotspot, and the CliRunner-based tests (test_cli.py ~969 lines) need import-path updates, a real regression window.

stress_test.dependency_check: click, pyyaml, python-dotenv, pydantic-ai confirmed in pyproject.toml. Commands-as-submodules on one click.Group is low-risk; group lookup is module-agnostic. But 'click lazy-loading' isn't a shipped feature -- a DIY subclass, understated as optional. 'resolve_model would return a TestModel' is wrong: it only special-cases greenpt:/infomaniak:/'||', passing 'test' through unchanged.
stress_test.migration_cost: Understated. Splitting cli.py into commands/{steps,pipeline,curation}.py + render.py touches every import path in the 969-line test_cli.py (admitted). Converting deferred per-command imports to module-level imports reintroduces the slow `dr --help` startup those deferred imports exist to avoid, unless the DIY lazy-Group is built first -- not sequenced into OCLI-01's migration steps.
stress_test.simpler_alternative: Skip the file-split/render.py restructuring; do the bug-bearing extractions inside cli.py as-is: persist_verify_outcome (OCLI-02, real bug fix), pipeline_options decorator (OCLI-05), enum-derived vocab (OCLI-06), reuse _resolve_claim_path in review (OCLI-03), exact-match the 'test' sentinel (OCLI-04), delete dead aliases (OCLI-08). Captures most risk reduction, no import-path churn.
stress_test.note: OCLI-02's premise checks out: cli.py's claim_refresh blocked/analyst-failed branches (~line 930-1000) omit failure=vr.failure that pipeline.py's onboard_entity passes (line 1986, 2047) -- a real bug the clean_slate rightly targets. The package-split half is directionally fine but oversells its cost and leans on one inaccurate claim about resolve_model.

clean_slates.title: Step-runner pipeline with a single claim-outcome persistence gateway
clean_slates.summary: Rebuild the orchestrator as small typed steps composed by one runner, with all claim/sidecar writes funneled through one outcome gateway and one generic checkpoint interface. The four entry points (verify, draft, onboard, refresh) become thin configurations of the same flow instead of four hand-written variants.
clean_slates.design: 1) A ClaimRun state object (claim text, resolved entity, config, accumulated sources/errors/failure) passed through pure-ish step functions: plan_research, dedup_urls, ingest, threshold_gate, analyze, audit. A single runner handles run_id binding, timeouts, null-body/rate-limit retries, and progress emission uniformly, so retry policy is written once instead of per-agent. 2) A persistence gateway: persist_outcome(run) classifies the terminal state (success | threshold_blocked | analyst_error | invalid_title) and performs claim + sidecar writes, including cached-source merging and failure propagation, in one module with public names. onboard_entity shrinks to entity lifecycle (verify name, enrich, screen templates) plus a loop of runner calls; claim-refresh in the CLI becomes runner + persist_outcome with reset_review=True. 3) Checkpoints collapse to one Gate.ask(request) method over typed request dataclasses (SourceReview, DisagreementReview, Choice[T]), so adding a gate adds a request type, not a method on every handler. 4) Claims live in one typed directory layout; entity refs have one grammar including drafts/.
clean_slates.tradeoffs: The generic runner adds indirection: debugging one claim means reading a dispatcher plus step functions instead of one linear script, and stack traces get one frame noisier. Typed gate requests are more ceremony than five plain methods. The migration itself is the biggest cost: on-disk YAML output ordering is effectively part of the diff-review workflow, so golden-file tests must be built first or churn will pollute research/ history. Entity onboarding's bespoke phases (verifier, enricher, disambiguation) don't benefit much and still carry most of their current complexity.

stress_test.dependency_check: Named deps (pydantic, pydantic-ai, httpx, click, PyYAML) all present in pipeline/pyproject.toml. But the design's own retry claim leans on _run_with_null_retry (pipeline.py:826), which catches openai.RateLimitError directly -- provider-coupled, not abstracted via pydantic-ai. 'openai' is omitted from the clean_slate dependency list despite being load-bearing.
stress_test.migration_cost: Understated. Frames it as swapping 4 hand-written entry points for thin configs, but onboard/enrich stay bespoke per its own tradeoffs paragraph -- only verify/draft/refresh actually share. Touches all of pipeline.py (2178 loc), persistence.py, checkpoints.py, cli.py at once; golden-file tests for YAML output ordering don't exist yet (test_orchestrator.py has 37 tests, no fixture-diff harness), so they're new work, not reuse.
stress_test.simpler_alternative: The findings list (ORCH-01/02/05/09/12) already is the 80% version: persist_outcome = the outcome gateway, _gather_sources extraction = the shared front-half, typed claim-dir layout and drafts/ ref grammar are itemized separately. All incremental, file-scoped, no new runner abstraction needed.
stress_test.note: Retry unification (the runner's main selling point) is already partly done via _run_with_null_retry, shared by verdict/analyst/auditor calls -- so that win is smaller than sold. The Gate.ask(request) checkpoint collapse relocates the 5-method branching into a 5-way match on request type rather than eliminating it; minor extensibility gain (new gate = new type, not a Protocol edit everywhere), offset by added ceremony. Net: right direction, but adopt the gateway/extraction pieces now and defer the generic step-runner and typed-gate rewrite until incremental extraction proves it's still needed.

clean_slates.title: Git-ledger research system: one generated schema, stateless step workers, static read model
clean_slates.summary: Rebuild keeps the three decisions that carry the project's mission (Markdown-in-Git as the auditable store, a fully static site, human-in-the-loop gates that never auto-resolve) and replaces the two that fight it: the hand-mirrored dual schema becomes one generated contract enforced at write time, and the monolithic orchestrator becomes small stateless step workers driven by claim state — the shape the repo's own vision doc already asks for.
clean_slates.design: (1) Contract: a single committed schema package (source of truth authored once — either Zod exported to JSON Schema or JSON Schema authored directly) from which the Python models/enums, the Astro Zod schemas, and the linter's field sets are generated; CI fails if any generated copy is stale. (2) Store: research/ stays Markdown+YAML in Git, but every write goes through one validated writer that (a) checks the schema before touching disk and (b) appends a transition record (agent, inputs, outputs, resulting state, checkpoint decisions) to the claim's sidecar — the sidecar becomes an append-only event log, and Git remains the outer audit layer. (3) Pipeline: four step workers (research, ingest, analyze, evaluate) each declaring a pre-condition on claim state and a post-condition; a thin driver (CLI today, cron later) finds claims matching a pre-condition and runs the step; verify-claim end-to-end is just the driver looping until a terminal state. Providers live behind one adapter owning retries, quirks, and per-call cost/energy accounting — which the mission (making AI cost visible) wants as a first-class output anyway. (4) Read model: unchanged — Astro collections compile the store to static pages, with the audit trail rendered from the event log; all projections live in lib functions, pages are markup.
clean_slates.tradeoffs: Codegen adds a toolchain: a broken generator blocks both languages, contributors must learn the regen step, and the generated Python is less idiomatic than hand-written enums. The append-only event log makes every pipeline run a bigger Git diff and a larger merge-conflict surface, and reviewers now read logs plus files instead of just files. Decomposed step workers destroy the single-stack-trace debugging experience: a failed run spans several state transitions, so triage tooling (dr-debug-blocked equivalents) must be built up front, not later — without it the rebuild is strictly worse to operate. Write-side validation fails earlier but harder: a schema nit now halts a pipeline run that the old system would have completed and flagged at next build. State-driven dispatch risks reinventing a workflow engine; the discipline is that pre/post-conditions stay in frontmatter fields that already exist (status, phase), not in a new runtime. Finally, the migration cost is concentrated exactly in the highest-churn files (pipeline.py, cli.py) and their test hotspots, so it competes directly with feature work for months.
dependencies: zod-to-json-schema (or direct JSON Schema authoring) + datamodel-code-generator for the Python side
gray-matter as the single TS frontmatter parser (already a devDependency)
GitHub Actions for the driver's scheduled 'observe/nudge' tick (optional, later)

stress_test.dependency_check: zod-to-json-schema, datamodel-code-generator, jsonschema are real but absent from package.json/pyproject.toml today (verified). gray-matter, pydantic-ai>=1.0, Astro collections correctly marked already-present/unchanged. Gap: models.py also holds hand-written provider logic (resolve_model, capability predicates) codegen can't produce; design doesn't say how that coexists with generated enums.
stress_test.migration_cost: Content corpus is small (5 claims, 36 sources) so data migration is cheap, but the code rewrite spans both hotspots (pipeline.py 2178 LOC, cli.py 2340 LOC, 47 test files), a new codegen toolchain, and a new event-log sidecar format. Design admits triage tooling must exist before write-side hard-fail ships or ops get worse, but gives no effort estimate. No phased rollout stated.
stress_test.simpler_alternative: Findings PAT-01 (schema-on-write) through PAT-04 (thin CLI/flows) already give scoped, sequenced fixes covering the contract-authority and orchestrator-decomposition value without the new transition-log/state-dispatch layer. That remaining piece is docs/architecture/vision-state-machine.md, which recommends Observe-only first and warns against premature full state-driven dispatch.
stress_test.note: No fictional dependencies; direction is sound and largely already-endorsed by the project's own vision-state-machine.md and PAT-01..04. But packaging it as one whole-system 'clean slate' skips past that doc's own staged, Observe-first rollout plan and understates codegen-toolchain and pre-built-triage-tooling costs as prerequisites, not side effects.

clean_slates.title: Three pure steps over a declared search-backend registry
clean_slates.summary: Rebuild the researcher as three individually-testable steps (plan, dispatch, score) composed by a thin runner, with every search backend living in tools/ behind one typed protocol and one shared HTTP-plumbing layer. Prompts move to instructions.md files like the rest of the pipeline.
clean_slates.design: tools/ holds brave.py, tavily.py, arxiv.py (later s2.py, openalex.py), each exposing async search(client, query, max_results) -> list[SearchHit] (one pydantic SearchHit replaces the ad-hoc dicts) plus a BACKEND descriptor: name, kind ('web'|'academic'), throttle rate, required env var. A module-level registry maps name -> descriptor; VerifyConfig validates search_backend and academic_origins against the registry in __post_init__, so misconfiguration fails at startup instead of silently mid-run. Shared plumbing (retry_after_seconds, token bucket per registered backend, HTTP_READ_S) lives in common/, registered once from the registry - no per-client boilerplate. decomposed.py shrinks to a runner over three step functions: plan_step (planner agent, timeout->StepError mapping, returns PlanStepResult with its trace fragment), dispatch_step (fan-out over jobs = [(origin, query, coro)] with first-contributor-wins dedup, returns candidates + acquisition entries), and score_step (scorer agent, with an explicit FallbackPolicy object that keeps only primary/secondary candidates capped at max_sources and flags the trace as unscored). The runner concatenates trace fragments into ResearchOutput; fallback and commit logic are module-level and unit-tested directly. Planner/scorer/verifier/enricher prompts live in researcher/instructions/*.md loaded via load_instructions, per-entity-type sections as fragments; the verifier and enricher share one prompt builder parameterized by label and sections.
clean_slates.tradeoffs: More indirection: a registry plus protocol for three backends is ceremony the current if/else avoids, and readers must hop between descriptor, registry, and client to trace one search. Typed SearchHit forces touching every test that currently fakes dict results, and splitting the runner spreads audit-trace assembly across step results, so the end-to-end sidecar shape is harder to see in one screen. The migration itself churns the subsystem's rank-6 hotspot, risking regressions in the well-tested fallback edge cases; the honest scorer fallback also changes observable behavior (fewer sources ingested on scorer failure), which needs operator sign-off, and startup validation turns previously-tolerated config into hard failures for existing scripts.

stress_test.dependency_check: httpx/pydantic/pydantic-ai/stdlib ElementTree already in pipeline/pyproject.toml, no new deps needed. But common/instructions.py's load_instructions(agent_dir) always loads a literal 'instructions.md' from one directory (confirmed: analyst/, ingestor/, auditor/ each hold exactly one, one agent per package). Four named files in one researcher/instructions/ dir isn't supported without changing that function's signature first.
stress_test.migration_cost: Tradeoffs section is honestly self-critical (hotspot churn, behavior change, stricter startup validation) but misses two touchpoints: orchestrator/pipeline.py:1372 imports search_brave directly for the collision probe and consumes raw dicts, so it must move to the typed protocol too; and every backend test currently faking dict results needs a SearchHit rewrite, not just decomposed.py's tests.
stress_test.simpler_alternative: Split decomposed_research into plan/dispatch/score step functions (fixes the real hotspot, RSR-02) plus a shared retry_after_seconds helper + brave throttle + HTTP_READ_S everywhere (RSR-04). Skip the SearchHit/protocol/registry layer: VerifyConfig already validates search_backend against a plain frozenset (_KNOWN_BACKENDS); extend that for academic_origins instead of building a full descriptor registry for 3 backends.
stress_test.note: Direction matches well-evidenced findings (RSR-02/04/05/08/09) and no exotic dependency is required. But the registry+protocol+SearchHit layer is ceremony for 3 backends when a frozenset-style validation extension already exists as precedent, and the instructions.md claim doesn't match the actual one-file-per-package API. Adopt the step-split and shared-plumbing pieces; drop or justify the registry before building it.

clean_slates.title: Writer-owned contract with generated mirrors
clean_slates.summary: The pipeline writes every research file, so the pipeline owns the schema: Pydantic models are the single definition, and everything the site needs (Zod validation, TS vocab types, label maps, docs tables) is generated or CI-verified from them. The site keeps hand-written schemas only for content it authors itself (resources).
clean_slates.design: 1) pipeline/common/contract/ holds Pydantic models for claim frontmatter, source frontmatter, entity frontmatter, criteria entries, and the audit sidecar; persistence.py serializes exclusively through them. 2) A `dr contract export` command emits JSON Schema files plus a vocab.json (enum values + reader-facing labels/glosses, which live as enum metadata on the Python side) into a committed contract/ directory. 3) The Astro side validates research collections against the exported JSON Schema via a tiny loader shim (Ajv), or via Zod schemas generated at dev time; src/lib vocab modules (verdict labels, verification gloss, topic labels) are generated from vocab.json, deleting the four hand-mirrored files. 4) CI fails if `dr contract export` produces a diff, which replaces every 'edit all three together' comment and the grep-based drift tests. 5) auditSchema disappears as a hand-written artifact; the sidecar contract is exactly the Pydantic model, and unknown keys are a build error on both sides. 6) The claims loader is a standard glob loader plus a separate audits collection; the join happens in the one page that renders the audit trail. 7) resources/matrix schemas stay hand-written Zod in src/ since the site is their writer, with per-layout discriminated-union validation at build time.
clean_slates.tradeoffs: Adds a codegen/export step and a committed generated directory: contributors must rerun an export after model changes, and generated TS is less pleasant to read than hand-written Zod. JSON Schema cannot express the current superRefine cross-field checks, so those become paired custom validators (Pydantic model_validator + a small TS check) — one rule, two enforcement sites, though now both are tested. Type inference on the site gets slightly weaker unless Zod generation (rather than Ajv) is chosen. For a repo this small the machinery is arguably heavier than the ten enums it protects; the payoff only materializes if the planned research-repo separation happens, at which point the exported contract becomes the interface between two repos and the investment is exactly right.

stress_test.dependency_check: pydantic (BaseModel, model_json_schema) is real and already used pipeline-side (pyproject.toml). zod isn't a direct npm dep but is legitimately re-exported via astro:content (verified). Ajv is NOT currently a dependency - net new. No Pydantic-to-Zod codegen library exists anywhere in the repo; that piece is unbuilt, from scratch.
stress_test.migration_cost: Unlike every SCH-* finding, clean_slate gives no migration steps. Today only sources have a Pydantic frontmatter model (model_dump); claims/entities/audit sidecar are hand-assembled dicts. Needs new contract module, 5 models, new CLI cmd, Ajv-or-codegen loader. superRefine cross-field checks can't come from JSON Schema, so paired Python+TS validators remain - undercutting 'single definition'.
stress_test.simpler_alternative: SCH-02's own fix (shared src/lib/vocab.ts + promote existing enum_drift.py into CI) and SCH-01's own fix (one Sidecar Pydantic model + matching Zod fields) already capture most of the drift-prevention value today with zero new dependencies and no export/codegen machinery.
stress_test.note: Direction is sound and the design is unusually honest about its own risk (repo this small, machinery may exceed the ten enums it protects) and correctly ties payoff to the planned research-repo split. But apply it later/selectively: the file's own smaller findings (SCH-01/02/04) deliver most of the value now, using only dependencies already present.

clean_slates.title: One gate, one data source, promoted artifacts
clean_slates.summary: Rebuilt today, this subsystem collapses to a single canonical quality gate invoked identically by developers and CI, one redirect data module feeding both Astro and Cloudflare, and a deploy that promotes the already-verified build artifact instead of rebuilding. Ad hoc operational scripts become a small parameterized ops/ toolkit; one-shot migrations never live next to durable tooling.
clean_slates.design: tasks.py stays the single entry point: `inv check` = astro build, markdownlint, `dr lint --severity error`, pytest unit. package.json keeps only leaf scripts (dev/build/preview); its 'check' chain and check-citations.ts are deleted, with citation integrity owned solely by the pipeline linter. ci.yml becomes two jobs: (1) gate - setup-node + astral-sh/setup-uv, `uv tool install invoke`, `inv check`, with a conditional dist/ artifact upload when called from deploy; (2) annotate - parses dr lint's JSON into PR annotations. deploy.yml calls ci.yml with upload-dist=true and deploys the artifact; no second build. Redirects live in src/lib/redirects.ts, imported by astro.config.ts and compiled to redirects.json by a checked generator that enforces slashless canonical targets. scripts/ shrinks to seo/ (three scripts sharing a token helper, URL lists as data files), ops/onboard-entity.sh + ops/clear-entity.sh (parameterized, citation-aware deletion), and publish-graphify.sh (copy + noindex + assertion); graph.html is injected into dist/ at deploy time rather than committed. Finished migrations like rerun_v1_claims.py are deleted on completion, their semantics promoted into dr flags if still wanted.
clean_slates.tradeoffs: CI gains a bootstrap dependency on invoke and uv, and a tasks.py bug can now break CI, not just local runs. Collapsing to one gate job serializes build/lint/test that today run in two parallel jobs, so wall-clock PR feedback may get slower unless the gate is split back into invoke subtask jobs (re-adding some YAML). Promoting the artifact means the deployed dist/ is built in the gate job's environment, so any gate/deploy environment differences vanish silently instead of failing loudly. Deploy-time injection of graph.html makes the published graph unreproducible from a plain checkout.

stress_test.dependency_check: astral-sh/setup-uv and workflow_call conditional dist upload are real, valid GHA features; uv auto-syncs dev deps so no explicit 'uv sync --dev' needed. But the gate job spec omits 'npm ci' before 'inv check' (build fails without it), and deploy-pages picking up an artifact uploaded inside a nested reusable-workflow job is asserted, not verified.
stress_test.migration_cost: Undercounted: clean_slate fuses ~8 separate findings (CI job merge, redirect SSOT+generator, ops/ toolkit, seo script refactor, graph deploy-injection, rerun script deletion) into one 'rebuild' with no combined sequencing, though each finding individually lists a small/medium migration. Realistically 6-8 staged PRs, several touching the live Pages deploy path.
stress_test.simpler_alternative: Ship SCI-01 (add pytest job), SCI-03 (delete check-citations.ts + tsx/gray-matter deps), SCI-09 (version sync) now; each has a safe standalone migration already in findings. Defer the CI job-merge and build-once/promote-artifact until nested-artifact pickup is verified on a throwaway branch; keep two parallel CI jobs meanwhile.
stress_test.note: The 'graph.html injected into dist/ at deploy time' claim is unfounded: graphify-out/ is git-ignored and only produced by an interactive local graphify skill run (docs/architecture/graphify.md), not by anything CI can invoke. That piece contradicts the design's own SCI-06 finding. Rest (single gate, redirect single source of truth) is directionally sound but presented as more atomic than it is.

clean_slates.title: Server-first component kit with one type source and root-scoped islands
clean_slates.summary: Rebuild the library around three rules: every data-driven component imports its payload type from the zod schemas that already validate the content; every interactive component scopes its behavior to its own root element; every shared visual (chips, pill-nav, return-top, sr-only) is defined exactly once. The components themselves mostly survive; the wiring between them is what gets replaced.
clean_slates.design: (1) Types: content.config.ts (or a src/lib/contentTypes.ts wrapper) exports z.infer types for matrix, guide, and tool payloads; components take typed props, and resources/[...slug].astro parses every layout's data with its schema, not just matrix. (2) Styles: tokens.css stays; global.css gains the full chip family (kind-* and verdict-* skins) and the canonical .sr-only; new ReturnTop and PillNav components own their markup, styles, and the stuck-height observer; resources.css shrinks to wallpaper/grain/hero decor. (3) Behavior: a 10-line mountIslands helper runs init(root) for each [data-island] element; FilterBar/FacetBar and the RA filter chips all follow the initMatrix root-scoping pattern, with events dispatched on the island root. (4) Logic: parseInline/stripMd, decision-tree scoring, and facet matching live in src/lib/ with vitest coverage; the decision tree server-renders all steps as hidden sections and its client script only toggles visibility and fills result numbers. (5) A11y: one a11yPrefs.ts module feeds both the pre-paint inline script (via define:vars) and A11yControl, computing effective motion identically in both.
clean_slates.tradeoffs: Coupling component types to content.config's zod schemas cuts against the planned research-repo separation; the schema module would have to move with the content or be published as a tiny shared package. Promoting chip/pill styles to global.css gives up Astro's scoped-style guarantee, so naming discipline replaces compiler isolation and a careless global rule can now leak. Server-rendering every decision-tree step ships roughly all step markup to every visitor of that one page and requires care that hidden sections stay out of the accessibility tree and search snippets. Adding vitest introduces a test toolchain to a site that has lived on build-as-test, which is real maintenance surface for a solo maintainer.

stress_test.dependency_check: Mostly sound: astro:content re-exports zod (verified, no zod devDep needed), lucide-astro/Astro 6.1.8 present, define:vars already used (FilterBar). Gap: 'one a11yPrefs.ts module feeds both' scripts is overstated -- define:vars serializes data not functions, so effectiveMotion() logic can't be truly shared without duplicating code or losing the pre-paint script's synchronous timing.
stress_test.migration_cost: Understated as a unified whole: touches ~20 existing files plus ~6 new ones (PillNav, ReturnTop, a11yPrefs.ts, shouldI.ts, inlineMd.ts, mountIslands helper) across 1 large + 4 medium + 5 small independently-scoped changes (SC-01..SC-11). Individually each migration step is well-evidenced and low-risk; bundled as 'clean slate' it reads smaller than the sum of its parts.
stress_test.simpler_alternative: Skip the 'clean slate' framing entirely and execute SC-01 through SC-11 as normal incremental refactors in severity order (SC-04 first, then the small dedup wins SC-02/03/05/06/09, then SC-01/07/08, defer SC-11 vitest until logic is extracted). Same end state, no speculative mountIslands abstraction built ahead of need, no overstated a11y-module unification.
stress_test.note: This isn't a speculative rewrite -- it's a reassembly of the doc's own already-evidenced findings (SC-01..SC-11) into one narrative, which is why it's low-risk relative to typical 'rebuild' proposals. Main correction needed: the a11yPrefs sharing claim between is:inline and module-scoped scripts, and honest sizing of aggregate effort.

clean_slates.title: Thin routes over a shared page kit
clean_slates.summary: Rebuild the pages layer as thin route files (data plumbing only) over a small shared kit: one nav/IA module derived from content collections, a split Base shell, and deterministic, testable presentation logic. Structured data (FAQ, ClaimReview, SearchAction) is generated from the same data the visible page renders, never hand-copied.
clean_slates.design: 1) src/lib/site.ts owns the IA: nav sections built from static config plus getCollection('resources'); both the nav bar and the /research numbered index render from it. 2) Base.astro shrinks to the document shell; Head.astro (meta/OG/JSON-LD/theme boot), SiteNav.astro (variant 'bar'|'overlay' — one burger implementation), SiteFooter.astro. 3) All JSON-LD flows through builders in src/lib/jsonld.ts that take the same objects the templates render (buildFaqSchema(faqs), buildClaimReview(claim)), making drift structurally impossible and letting a build check validate every emitted block. 4) The three entity index routes become one EntityIndexGrid component call each; detail routes keep their file-routing paths but their bodies are components (ClaimDetail, SourceDetail, EntityDetail) so each route file is under ~50 lines of getStaticPaths + lookup. 5) The homepage scatter is a HeroScatter island: pure seeded geometry in src/lib/scatter.ts (seed = hash of highlighted claim ids, so builds are reproducible and the layout changes only when content does), glitch animation in a bundled src/scripts/hero-glitch.ts, titles escaped before term-bolding. 6) Shared micro-helpers: isoDate(), truncateAtWord(), escapeHtml() in src/lib. 7) Freshness dates come from frontmatter (updatedDate), not git subprocesses.
clean_slates.tradeoffs: More files and one more layer of indirection on a site with ~20 routes — for a solo operator, jumping between route file and body component is real friction. Parameterized index pages make bespoke per-type tweaks slightly harder, and the homepage's hand-tuned character is easier to accidentally flatten once its pieces are 'reusable'. The migration itself churns the two highest-churn hotspots (Base.astro, index.astro), so regressions during the split are the main risk; deterministic scatter also means the hero layout stops varying between deploys, which loses a bit of the intended 'fresh scatter' feel (though per-visitor randomness was never real — positions were always frozen per build).
dependencies: Astro content collections (astro:content, already in use)
Zod schema validation (already in use via content.config)
a ~10-line seeded PRNG (mulberry32-style, inlined; no new package)

stress_test.dependency_check: No phantom deps: astro:content, zod (via content.config), @astrojs/sitemap all in package.json; seeded PRNG is 10 lines, no package needed. Wording is imprecise though: 'HeroScatter island' implies a client framework but none is installed (it's a static component + bundled script, which is fine); theme-boot script must stay is:inline through the Head split or theme-flash (FOUC) returns.
stress_test.migration_cost: Design does name the regression risk (churns Base.astro + index.astro, the two highest-churn files) so it's not dishonest, but it's incomplete: no sequencing plan for landing ~8 findings (SP-01,02,03,05,06,08,09,12) on two overlapping files without collisions, and no explicit call-out of the FOUC trap in the Head split.
stress_test.simpler_alternative: Land SP-01 through SP-12 finding-by-finding as scoped in-place refactors (already how they're written), verifying after each. Skip clean_slate point 4 (splitting research-detail routes into ClaimDetail/SourceDetail/EntityDetail components) and the ClaimReview jsonld.ts builder — no finding evidences duplication or drift there; community_check even says 'agree' for that unit as-is.
stress_test.note: Point 4 is the real overreach: it adds indirection across 5 detail-route files with zero evidenced payback (only FAQ, SP-06, has documented drift). The FAQ single-source fix itself is sound — one faqs array feeding both <details> and JSON-LD genuinely eliminates that drift class, not just papers over it.

clean_slates.title: Factory-backed test pyramid with a CI gate and auto-derived CLI coverage
clean_slates.summary: Rebuilt today, the suite keeps its strong bones (respx HTTP tests, marker-gated acceptance layer, byte-level file assertions) but gains three structural pieces it currently lacks: a single factory module, an injectable model seam so tests stop monkeypatching pydantic_ai, and a CI job with per-command coverage that new CLI commands cannot escape.
clean_slates.design: Four layers. (1) pipeline/tests/factories.py: claim/sidecar/entity writers, ResearchOutput and StepError builders, canned TestModel factories for all six agents, and a trimmed fixture templates.yaml — no test file defines its own data builders. (2) Unit layer pinned on public seams: VerifyConfig grows a model_factory (default resolve_model); tests inject TestModels through config instead of patch.object(Agent, 'override'); prompt builders, Pydantic validators, linter checks, and the StepError-vocab drift guard stay as-is. (3) Behavior layer: CliRunner tests generated per registered command by iterating main.commands — every command gets a --help assertion automatically and a hand-written happy-path invocation; step-* recovery commands get tests against extracted, named functions rather than inline mirrors of click handlers. (4) Acceptance layer unchanged (marker + key-gated skipif is already right). CI: a pytest job (-m 'not acceptance', pytest-cov with a floor on orchestrator/) runs beside the existing content-lint job; the acceptance suite stays local/manual. llm-tester survives as a tracked diagnostic with its matrix single-sourced in tester.py.
clean_slates.tradeoffs: Factory indirection makes individual tests less self-contained — a reader must hop to factories.py to see fixture shapes, and factory defaults can hide what a given test actually depends on. The model_factory seam adds production API surface that exists mainly for tests. Auto-derived per-command tests guarantee breadth but invite shallow assertions that look like coverage; the happy-path bodies still need human judgment. A coverage floor on a 2,340-line cli.py will initially fail and forces either test-writing work upfront or an embarrassingly low starting threshold. Migration is days of mechanical churn across 45 files with real risk of transcription errors in the ~30 duplicated helpers.

stress_test.dependency_check: All named deps are real and already exercised in-repo: respx, pydantic_ai 1.84.1 TestModel/Agent.override, click.testing.CliRunner, uv+GitHub Actions (lint-content job already does uv sync in pipeline/). Only pytest-cov is new but is a standard, low-risk addition. No fabricated APIs found.
stress_test.migration_cost: CI gate (TESTS-01) + smoke-test path fix (TESTS-09) are cheap, copying the existing lint-content job pattern almost verbatim. Factory consolidation is genuine mechanical churn across ~47 files (design says 45) with ~30 duplicated helpers, as the design itself admits. Coverage floor will fail on first run, also admitted.
stress_test.simpler_alternative: Ship the CI gate + smoke-test path fix + factories.py (TESTS-01/07/09) alone first: highest value, near-zero design risk, touches zero production code. Defer the model_factory DI seam and coverage floor to a follow-up once the keying bug below is resolved, instead of bundling a risky rearchitecture with the cheap CI win.
stress_test.note: Model_factory seam has a concrete bug: onboard_entity's entity_verifier_agent and entity_enricher_agent both resolve via cfg.model_for('researcher') (pipeline.py:1486/1623/1707) -- same spec string -- yet test_onboard.py needs distinct TestModels per agent (_verifier_model vs _enricher_model, lines 545-554). A factory keyed by resolved spec string collides; it must key by agent identity instead, which the design doesn't specify and adds more surface than described.

patterns.name: Pipes and Filters (staged pipeline)
patterns.defining_property: A fixed sequence of processing stages, each consuming the previous stage's output: research -> ingest -> threshold gate -> analyze -> evaluate, with each stage also runnable standalone as a dr step-* command.
patterns.assessment: Serving. The staged decomposition is the right shape for auditable LLM work: each stage has a typed output (ResearchOutput, SourceFile, AnalystOutput, ComparisonResult) and the step-* CLI commands prove the stages are conceptually separable. Hurting only in packaging: all filters are private functions fused into one 2.2k-LOC file (hotspot #1), so the pipes are function calls and the stages cannot be tested, replaced, or re-ordered without editing the monolith.
patterns.should_move_toward: Keep the pattern; move each filter into its own module (orchestrator/steps/research.py, ingest.py, analyze.py, evaluate.py) with an explicit input/output contract, leaving verify_claim as a thin composition function. The step-* commands then import the same modules the composed pipeline uses.
patterns.community_check: agree: graphify splits the in-scope code into 'Claim Verification Pipeline' (20), 'Source Threshold Gate' (24), 'Source URL Deduplication' (11), and 'Entity Onboarding Orchestrator' (75) — the graph already sees the stage seams that the single file hides.

patterns.name: Blackboard / filesystem-as-integration-bus
patterns.defining_property: Independent workers (pipeline agents, linter, CI scripts, Astro build) coordinate exclusively through a shared data store — Markdown+YAML files under research/ — with no direct calls between producer and consumer.

evidence.quote: File I/O for persisting research artifacts to disk.
Scan research/sources/*/*.md and return a url -> source_id mapping.
has a corresponding file at research/sources/<slug>.md

patterns.assessment: Serving, and it is the project's best architectural decision: Git history over the blackboard IS the audit trail, human review is a file diff, and the research repo can later split off (a stated goal). Hurting at the edges: because the bus is untyped files, every consumer brings its own parser and its own copy of the schema (see the schema-on-read and duplicated-gatekeeper entries), and the integration is invisible to import-graph tooling.
patterns.should_move_toward: Keep the blackboard. Harden its contract instead of replacing it: one schema artifact both sides consume, one frontmatter parser per language, and writes funneled through a single validated writer module (persistence.py is already almost that).
patterns.community_check: disagree (instructively): graphify groups by code proximity — 'Source Classification Persistence' (22), 'Content File Loader' (19), 'Citation Index Builder' (92), 'Astro Content Schema' (64) are separate communities with no edges through research/. The graph cannot see the filesystem bus, which confirms the integration is entirely out-of-band convention.

patterns.name: Schema-on-read without schema-on-write (missing anti-corruption/contract layer at the pipeline-site boundary)
patterns.defining_property: The authoritative schema lives in the reader (Zod, enforced at astro build); the writer assembles frontmatter as hand-built dicts with no validation against that schema, and the Python side's knowledge of the contract is a hand-maintained mirror rather than a shared artifact.

evidence.quote: validates all frontmatter against the Zod schemas
Shared enums mirroring the Zod schemas in src/content.config.ts.
`sec_cik` shipped via source-pool-expansion-tier1.md without a linter add

patterns.assessment: Hurting. A pipeline write that violates the contract is not caught when it happens; it surfaces minutes-to-days later as an astro build failure or a lint warning, far from the causing code. The contract itself exists in at least four hand-synchronized copies (Zod schema, Python enum mirror, linter key sets, content-model.md tables). The linter's own comment records the failure mode already occurring: sec_cik shipped without the linter copy being updated. enum-drift.json shows the 10 enum pairs are in sync today only by manual discipline.
patterns.should_move_toward: Pick one schema authority and generate the rest. Cheapest path: export JSON Schema from the Zod definitions at build time (zod-to-json-schema), commit it, validate every frontmatter dict against it inside serialize_frontmatter/persistence before writing (true schema-on-write), and generate the Python enums plus the linter's canonical key sets from the same artifact. The Zod boundary then becomes a real anti-corruption layer instead of a tripwire.
patterns.community_check: agree: graphify puts the two sides in separate communities — 'Shared Enum Models' (42) and 'Astro Content Schema' (64) — with no connecting edge; the mirror relationship exists only in docstrings, exactly the drift surface this entry names.

patterns.name: Leaky Abstraction at the provider gateway
patterns.defining_property: resolve_model exists to encapsulate LLM-provider concerns, but provider-specific failure handling (Infomaniak null bodies, openai SDK exception types, per-model quirk sniffing by substring) lives in the orchestrator, so the encapsulation boundary does not hold.

evidence.quote: Run an agent, retrying on Infomaniak null-body responses.
if isinstance(exc, openai.RateLimitError) and attempt < retries:

patterns.assessment: Hurting. Every provider quirk fix lands in the repo's #1 hotspot (pipeline.py, churn 77) instead of the adapter that supposedly owns providers. The orchestrator cannot be read as provider-agnostic control flow, and adding a third provider (a GreenPT branch already exists) means auditing retry logic scattered across two files. Substring capability detection ("mistral" in model_id) is fragile against model renames.
patterns.should_move_toward: Move _run_with_null_retry, the null-body/rate-limit policy, and the quirk predicates into a provider adapter module (a run_agent(agent, prompt, timeout) facade next to resolve_model). Replace substring sniffing with a small declarative capability table keyed by provider:model. The orchestrator should not import openai.
patterns.community_check: agree: graphify already isolates 'Model Resolution Layer' (46) as its own community inside models.py; the retry helpers in pipeline.py fall into the pipeline community instead — the graph shows the provider concern split across two communities that should be one.

patterns.name: Strategy (model resolution and search backends)
patterns.defining_property: Interchangeable algorithms selected by a spec string at runtime: provider-prefixed model specs (greenpt:, infomaniak:, || fallback chains) resolve to different clients, and the researcher dispatches to brave/tavily backends with graceful fallback.
patterns.assessment: Serving. Spec strings compose well with CLI flags and env vars (DR_MODEL, RESEARCH_SEARCH_BACKEND), fallback chains via || are a genuinely nice operator affordance, and unknown backends fail soft with a warning. The implementation is an if/elif chain rather than a registry — at two providers and two backends that is the correct amount of machinery; do not add a plugin framework yet. The weak spot is that the strategies are selected cleanly but their failure behavior is not owned by them (see the leaky-abstraction entry).
patterns.should_move_toward: Keep the if-chain until a third provider lands, then convert to a dict of prefix -> factory. Fold the per-model quirk predicates into each strategy's factory so a strategy carries its own capabilities.
patterns.community_check: agree: 'Model Resolution Layer' (46) is a distinct graphify community despite sharing a file with the enums, matching this pattern's boundary.

patterns.name: God File (orchestrator pipeline and CLI)
patterns.defining_property: Two files concentrate most of the subsystem's logic and churn: pipeline.py holds the verify pipeline, the persistence flow (research_claim), entity onboarding (onboard_entity, enrich_entity), and retry policy; cli.py holds 15+ commands with inline wiring. They are hotspots #1 and #2.

evidence.quote: Unified dr CLI with subcommands for the full pipeline.
There is no monolithic orchestrator that "runs the pipeline."

patterns.assessment: Hurting, and the repo's own vision doc names the target shape this violates: 'composable, not orchestrated' with no monolithic orchestrator, while pipeline.py is precisely that monolith (2178 LOC, churn 77, betweenness 0.43). Every feature — a new acquisition origin, a sidecar field, an onboarding tweak — edits the same file, so merge risk and review load concentrate there. cli.py compounds it: command bodies contain async wiring and result printing instead of delegating.
patterns.should_move_toward: Split pipeline.py along the seams graphify already sees: steps/ (the four filters + threshold gate), flows/verify.py (research_claim), flows/onboard.py (onboard_entity + enrichment), and a provider-adapter module for the retry policy. cli.py commands become thin: parse options, build VerifyConfig, call a flow function, print via a shared reporter.
patterns.community_check: agree: graphify finds six-plus communities inside the two files ('Claim Verification Pipeline' 20, 'Claim Verification Models' 0, 'Entity Onboarding Orchestrator' 75, 'Source Threshold Gate' 24, 'CLI Command Router' 9, 'Claim Statistics Reporter' 7) — the graph's decomposition is finer than the file layout, which is the definition of a god file.

patterns.name: Shotgun Surgery (manual keep-in-sync protocol)
patterns.defining_property: Single conceptual changes require coordinated edits in several files, and the codebase knows it: multiple comments explicitly instruct future editors to synchronize by hand.

evidence.quote: The returned dict keys must stay in sync with _build_source_dict in pipeline.py.
editing this tuple and the matching VerifyConfig fields.

patterns.assessment: Hurting. Adding one claim frontmatter field touches content.config.ts, checks.py's CANONICAL_CLAIM_KEYS, persistence.py's _write_claim_file signature and fm dict, content-model.md, and sometimes models.py — five-plus files across two languages. Adding an agent means editing AGENT_NAMES plus matching VerifyConfig fields plus CLI options. The comments are honest, but a comment is not an enforcement mechanism; the sec_cik linter miss shows the protocol failing in practice. The one bright spot: test_step_error_vocab.py mechanically enforces one of these contracts, proving the team knows the better pattern.
patterns.should_move_toward: Replace each keep-in-sync comment with either (a) a single source of truth the copies derive from (schema codegen for the field sets and enums; a dataclass of per-agent settings iterated by the CLI instead of parallel fields), or (b) a drift test in the style of test_step_error_vocab.py where codegen is overkill. Every remaining hand-sync comment should be treated as a defect, not documentation.
patterns.community_check: agree: the synchronized copies land in different graphify communities (42 enums, 64 Astro schema, linter community, pipeline community) with no edges between them — drift between communities is invisible to any structural tool, which is why it needs generation or tests.

patterns.name: Parallel Hierarchies (docs/roles vs packages/files)
patterns.defining_property: The documented role vocabulary and the code layout are two hierarchies that must be mentally mapped onto each other: the Evaluator role lives in auditor/, a documented Router has no package, and researcher/agent.py contains no agent (it is the Brave search client, while sibling clients live in researcher/tools/).

evidence.quote: Brave Web Search client used by the decomposed researcher.
The Evaluator role is implemented in `pipeline/auditor/`; the role and package names diverge intentionally in v1.

patterns.assessment: Hurting, disproportionately for an agent-operated repo: every AI agent session pays the Evaluator/auditor translation tax, and sidecar fields (auditor_verdict) bake the wrong name into published data the longer it waits. researcher/agent.py is a double fake-out — named like the PydanticAI agent files in analyst/ and ingestor/ but holding a search client that belongs in researcher/tools/ next to tavily.py and arxiv.py. The Router row documents a package that does not exist. Each divergence is individually small and self-flagged; collectively they mean the docs cannot be trusted as a map.
patterns.should_move_toward: Do the deferred renames as one mechanical commit early post-v1: auditor/ -> evaluator/ (with a versioned sidecar field migration), researcher/agent.py -> researcher/tools/brave.py, and either delete the Router row's package column or create the package stub. Until then, the divergences should live in exactly one table, not be re-explained per doc.
patterns.community_check: agree: graphify labels the relevant community 'Auditor Agent Bundle' (26) — the tool independently adopted the package name, not the documented role name, demonstrating how the code-side hierarchy wins and the docs-side vocabulary loses.

patterns.name: Static Site Generation as a CQRS-style read model
patterns.defining_property: Writes (pipeline + operator commits into research/) and reads (Astro build compiling collections into denormalized static pages, filtered to published) are fully separated models; the read model is rebuilt from scratch on every deploy and serves no live queries.

evidence.quote: const allClaims = await getCollection('claims', ({ data }) => data.status === 'published');
All routes are statically generated at build time via `getStaticPaths()`.

patterns.assessment: Serving. Zero runtime attack surface, free hosting, and the full-rebuild read model means no cache-invalidation class of bugs; the custom claims-with-audit loader is a clean projection that joins claim + sidecar at read time instead of denormalizing on the write side. The pattern's known cost (rebuild latency growing with content volume) is irrelevant at current scale and acceptable for years.
patterns.should_move_toward: Keep. The only discipline needed: projections (joins, filters, derived maps like entityNameMap) should live in src/lib/ query helpers shared across pages, not be re-derived inside each page's frontmatter script — several pages re-filter status === 'published' independently, which is a one-line-per-page drift risk (a page forgetting the filter would publish drafts).
patterns.community_check: agree: 'Astro Content Schema' (64) and 'Astro Base Layout' (73) are coherent read-side communities cleanly separated from all pipeline communities; graphify shows no write-path code in any site community.

patterns.name: Human-in-the-Loop Checkpoint (workflow interception protocol)
patterns.defining_property: Named interception points (review_sources, review_disagreement, review_onboard, entity disambiguation/enrichment) defined as a Protocol, with an auto-approve implementation for tests and a CLI implementation for interactive runs; disagreements are open-loop and surface to the operator rather than being auto-resolved.

evidence.quote: Return True to proceed to analysis, False to halt.

patterns.assessment: Serving, and well-executed: the Protocol keeps the pipeline testable (AutoApprove) while making human gates first-class, which is the core trust proposition of the site. Weakness: checkpoint decisions are transient booleans — a proceed/halt at review_sources leaves no durable record in the audit sidecar, so the audit trail shows what agents did but not what the human waved through mid-run. The vision doc's principle 2 (transitions as first-class records) already names this gap.
patterns.should_move_toward: Persist each checkpoint outcome (which gate, decision, timestamp, handler type) into the audit sidecar's pipeline_run block. Keep the Protocol; resist expanding return types beyond what each gate needs.
patterns.community_check: agree: 'Human Review Checkpoints' (14) and 'CLI Checkpoint Handlers' (107) are distinct graphify communities matching the protocol/implementation split.

patterns.name: Big Ball of Mud check (verdict: absent globally; localized page monolith)
patterns.defining_property: The system as a whole is NOT a Big Ball of Mud — layering (agents / orchestrator / common / content store / site) is real and enforced by direction-of-import. The mud is localized: index.astro fuses data assembly, content transformation (regex entity-bolding), scatter layout math, and JSON-LD into one 1k-LOC page file.

patterns.assessment: Mostly reassuring: the honest adversarial answer to 'is any area a Big Ball of Mud?' is no — even the god files are structured monoliths with docstrings and seams, not mud. The homepage is the closest approach: boldInTitle does regex HTML injection over claim titles inline in a page template, wedge/scatter layout logic lives beside it, and none of it is reusable or unit-testable where it sits.
patterns.should_move_toward: Extract boldInTitle and the scatter-item assembly into src/lib/ (testable pure functions), leaving index.astro as layout + markup. This mirrors what src/lib/verdict.ts already does for verdict labels, so it is following an established in-repo pattern, not inventing one.
patterns.community_check: partially agree: graphify's site-pages communities ('Astro Base Layout' 73, 'Verdict Sorting Utilities' 78) capture the extracted utilities but index.astro's inline logic forms no coherent community of its own — unextracted page logic is structurally invisible, consistent with the monolith diagnosis.
